arguments.description: Links this key to a connected app's install. Revoking the install or its grant for this key's environment revokes the key. The install must be active and authorized for that environment. Set only at creation; it never changes. Omit for an unlinked key. Keys created by a linked key inherit its link. Each install can have up to 25 linked keys that have not been revoked per environment.

arguments.name: sandbox_id
arguments.description: Public ID of the sandbox the new test key is bound to. A live credential or a user session sends it to create a test key in that sandbox, and omits it for a live key. A Dashboard or onboarding session may name any of the merchant's active sandboxes, and an onboarding session must send it: its first key goes to default_sandbox_id. Storage generation IDs are never accepted.

arguments.name: scopes
arguments.description: The scopes to grant. Required only with access restricted; forbidden with full or read_only. For a test key, use only scopes whose key_modes includes test in x-flint-scopes. The developer.sandboxes.read and developer.sandboxes.write scopes are valid on test keys; developer.partner_apps.read and developer.partner_apps.write are live-only.

arguments.name: checkout_session_id
arguments.description: Flint checkout session ID.

arguments.name: expected_version
arguments.description: Optional expected version of this resource. A stale value returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with the current version. Retrieve the resource and rebuild the request before retrying.

arguments.name: reason_message
arguments.description: Your note explaining why you are closing the checkout session. It is not shown to the buyer.

arguments.name: input
arguments.description: JSON body: FILE.json, - for stdin, or inline JSON

arguments.name: customer_id
arguments.description: Existing customer to link to the order Flint creates. Not allowed with type: order: the session uses the order's customer, so set customer_id on the order first.

arguments.name: delivery_method_ids
arguments.description: Immutable delivery method assignment for this checkout, 1 to 25 unique IDs. Omit it to use settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids when the order has items to deliver; otherwise no methods are assigned. Empty arrays and null are rejected.

arguments.name: expires_in_seconds
arguments.description: Seconds the session stays open, from 60 to 86,400. Omit it to use settings.checkout.default_expires_in_seconds, or 24 hours.

arguments.name: external_reference_id
arguments.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

arguments.name: inventory_reservation_ids
arguments.description: Merchant-created cart holds this session may adopt during delivery selection. Only with type: order and a merchant credential. At most 100 unique IDs; exceeding the cap returns INVALID_REQUEST with param inventory_reservation_ids. Immutable after creation. Buyer quotes credit still-eligible bound holds and buyer selections adopt matching units without supplying IDs. Merchant delivery requests that omit IDs also use this binding; explicit IDs, including an empty array, replace it for that request. First adopter wins when sessions share a hold. Unused units remain held until released or expired. Unknown or ineligible IDs at creation return 404. Invalidated or otherwise ended sessions cannot use the binding, and replacement sessions never inherit it.

arguments.name: invoice_id
arguments.description: The open invoice whose balance due now this checkout collects. An open session for the invoice's current collection is reused and returned with 200. Required when type is invoice, and not allowed otherwise.

arguments.name: invoice_schedule_entry_id
arguments.description: Optional. The schedule entry to collect. Only the earliest entry that is due and still has an outstanding balance can be collected; omit it to collect that entry. Not allowed on an invoice without a schedule. Only with type invoice.

arguments.name: order_id
arguments.description: The order to collect. It must be open and not collected by an invoice or a return resolution.

arguments.name: page_origin
arguments.description: Origin of the page where you render this headless checkout, such as https://shop.example.com. Only this origin can show the checkout's gift card challenge and receive its result. It does not let the browser call the Flint API. Accepted only when surface is headless. Use HTTPS and a lowercase DNS hostname. Do not include a path, query, fragment, or default port. In test mode, localhost, names ending in .localhost, and 127.0.0.1 also work over HTTP or HTTPS.

arguments.name: payment_return_url
arguments.description: Headless sessions only. Absolute HTTPS URL on your site where Flint sends the buyer after a redirect payment such as Affirm, whatever the outcome; read the session there to show the result. Required when the session offers affirm. It can't contain credentials, a query string, or a fragment. Test mode also accepts http loopback URLs. Up to 2,048 characters.

arguments.name: replace_checkout_session_id

commands.name: me.checkout-sessions.create
commands.description: Create a checkout session for the current buyer

arguments.name: invoice_id
arguments.description: The open invoice whose balance due now this checkout collects. An open session for the invoice's current collection is reused and returned with 200. With an invoice access token, it must be the token's invoice; another invoice returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, and an invalid, expired or revoked token returns 401 INVALID_CREDENTIAL. With a customer session, it must be one of the buyer's invoices.

arguments.name: invoice_schedule_entry_id
arguments.description: Optional. The schedule entry to collect. Only the earliest entry that is due and still has an outstanding balance can be collected; omit it to collect that entry. Not allowed on an invoice without a schedule.

arguments.name: page_origin
arguments.description: Origin of the page where you render this headless checkout, such as https://shop.example.com. Only this origin can show the checkout's gift card challenge and receive its result. It does not let the browser call the Flint API. Accepted only when surface is headless. Use HTTPS and a lowercase DNS hostname. Do not include a path, query, fragment, or default port. In test mode, localhost, names ending in .localhost, and 127.0.0.1 also work over HTTP or HTTPS.

arguments.name: payment_return_url
arguments.description: Headless sessions only. Absolute HTTPS URL on your site where Flint sends the buyer after a redirect payment such as Affirm, whatever the outcome; read the session there to show the result. Required when the session offers affirm. It can't contain credentials, a query string, or a fragment. Test mode also accepts http loopback URLs. Up to 2,048 characters.

arguments.name: return_resolution_id
arguments.description: One of the buyer's return resolutions with a buyer payment pending on its replacement order. Another buyer's resolution, or an unknown one, returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. An open session with the same surface is reused and returned with 200.

arguments.name: return_url
arguments.description: Where the checkout sends the buyer after paying, such as the invoice's or Return's page in the customer account. Limited to 2048 characters (Unicode code points) before trimming surrounding whitespace. It must be an HTTPS address of the merchant's customer account: /{merchant_id} on Flint's account host, the merchant's active custom account domain, or the host of customer_account.merchant_account_url when the merchant hosts the account. In test mode, any URL on localhost or a loopback IP address (such as 127.0.0.1 or [::1]) is also accepted, over HTTP or HTTPS and on any port. Anything else returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST with an INVALID_VALUE detail on return_url. An alias for redirects.success_url on hosted checkout or payment_return_url on headless checkout; keep them consistent when sending both.

arguments.name: surface
arguments.description: Defaults to hosted. The same surface reuses the open checkout. A different surface replaces it only while no payment is in progress; otherwise the request returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason in_progress.

arguments.inference_hint: --invoice-id alone selects invoice; --invoice-schedule-entry-id alone selects invoice; --return-resolution-id alone selects return_resolution
arguments.name: type
arguments.description: What the checkout collects payment for. return_resolution: the buyer's balance on one of their return resolutions; send return_resolution_id. invoice: what is due now on one of the buyer's invoices; send invoice_id.

arguments.name: input
arguments.description: JSON body: FILE.json, - for stdin, or inline JSON

arguments.name: buyer_ip_address
arguments.description: The buyer's IP address, for risk screening, when your server pays on the buyer's behalf. Write-only.

arguments.name: client_action_type
arguments.description: How to complete the authentication step. Flint's API returns a Stripe client secret only for client_action_type stripe. A url action opens in a redirect, popup, or iframe; Stripe's authentication page receives what it needs to run the challenge, including the client secret for hosted 3DS2. If a payment is confirmed with a payment method Flint didn't approve, Flint doesn't count the charge, returns it to the buyer, and the payment intent ends canceled with cancellation_reason payment_returned. The Stripe secret can also confirm the payment with another card, so use it only with handleNextAction. Reader credentials do not support url; omit client_action_type or send stripe for reader payments. Defaults to stripe for a new confirmation; omission on a continuation keeps the existing type.

arguments.name: completion_behavior
arguments.description: What happens when the selected payment intents don't cover the balance. Defaults to complete_order.

arguments.name: expected_version
arguments.description: Optional version from the order you reviewed. A mismatch returns VERSION_CONFLICT, even when the outstanding amount is unchanged. Starting a payment advances the order's version. After a declined or failed attempt, use the order returned in the pay response or read the order again before retrying. When accepted_gift_card_allocation is sent, its order_version must match this value.

arguments.name: order_payment_attempt_id
arguments.description: Set order_payment_attempt_id.

arguments.name: payment_return_url
arguments.description: Where Flint sends the buyer after a redirect or authentication step, adding only payment_intent_id for a payment, or payment_method_id for a setup. The completion message uses type flint.payment_action.completed and exactly that one subject key. Without it, the step ends on a Flint page that tells the parent or opener the step completed. Accepts an absolute HTTPS URL or an app return URL with a custom scheme other than http, javascript, data, file, blob, or about. Cannot contain credentials, a query, or a fragment. Test mode also accepts HTTP loopback URLs. With a checkout credential on order pay, omit payment_return_url; checkout sessions use their own configured return URL.

arguments.name: save_payment_method
arguments.description: The buyer's choice to save the card they typed for faster checkout at this merchant. Send true only from the checkout session's own credential, when the session's can_save_payment_method is true, for one newly collected card sent as stripe.confirmation_token created with setup_future_usage on_session. The card is saved with usage on_session once the payment succeeds, for the customer the checkout acts for: the customer the merchant created the session for, or the customer whose email the buyer confirmed in it. When save_payment_method_requires_verification is true, buyer_contact.email is required. The card is kept pending for the customer with that email, creating one if needed, and opens nothing until confirmed on the receipt within 24 hours. Without save_payment_method_phone, payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required is true and an emailed code confirms the save with purpose confirm_saved_payment_method and channel email. The code goes only to the email given with the payment. Subscription signup and setup still require email verification before collection when the email belongs to an existing customer. A checkout the buyer bound by a texted code saves the card with that number. A checkout whose buyer confirmed the customer's email can also send save_payment_method_phone, to save the card with a number the buyer confirms by text after paying. A checkout can send the buyer's choice with every payment button: Apple Pay, Google Pay, a bank account, or Affirm, in stripe.confirmation_token created with no setup_future_usage, pays without the save, and the payment attempt's payment_method_save reports not_saved with reason payment_method_not_saveable. The session's save_payment_method_types lists what is saved. Send false or omit it when the buyer does not choose to save; stripe.confirmation_token must then have no setup_future_usage.

arguments.name: save_payment_method_phone
arguments.description: A US or Canadian mobile phone number in E.164 format, such as +14155552671, that confirms a card saved while the checkout acts for no customer, or for the customer whose email the buyer confirmed in it. Send it with save_payment_method: true only from the checkout session's own credential, when the session's can_save_payment_method_with_phone is true. The card is kept for the customer the checkout acts for, or else the merchant's customer with the buyer's email, once the payment succeeds, or once it is approved when the merchant captures later, but works for nothing until the buyer confirms it within 24 hours, with a code texted to this number or, when the customer's email is the email of the payment, emailed there instead: request the code with POST /v1/checkout-sessions/{checkout_session_id}/customer-verifications and purpose confirm_saved_payment_method, and read payment_method_save on the checkout session. A card saved with the number makes it the customer's saved number, and the cards saved with the number it replaces are removed. A card not confirmed in time is not saved.

arguments.name: client_action_type
arguments.description: How to complete the authentication step. Flint's API returns a Stripe client secret only for client_action_type stripe. A url action opens in a redirect, popup, or iframe; Stripe's authentication page receives what it needs to run the challenge, including the client secret for hosted 3DS2. If a payment is confirmed with a payment method Flint didn't approve, Flint doesn't count the charge, returns it to the buyer, and the payment intent ends canceled with cancellation_reason payment_returned. Reader credentials do not support url; omit client_action_type or send stripe for reader payments. Defaults to stripe for a new confirmation; omission on a continuation keeps the existing type.

arguments.name: customer_presence
arguments.description: Whether the customer is present for this payment. Defaults to present. Send absent to charge a saved card while the customer is away, such as for a no-show fee, damages, or a top-up. Flint then sends the charge to the card network as merchant-initiated, using the card's stored credential, so the bank can't ask the customer to authenticate. absent can be sent only with an API key or partner token, and only for a saved card whose usage is off_session; a card the customer saved for checkout only returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason payment_method_not_reusable. If the bank still requires authentication, the payment fails with status requires_payment_method and last_payment_error.code authentication_required. Ask the customer to pay while present instead of retrying.

arguments.description: Return the platform fee on the payments this refund refunds, as Stripe's refund_application_fee does. By default the partner app keeps its fee. info.description: Flint's public /v1 API for payments, checkout, invoices, subscriptions, catalog, customers, returns, inventory, money movement, webhooks, and developer operations. Live keys and sandbox-bound test keys use the same API hostname; the key selects live or sandbox data. Keep ordinary secret API keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception. A request body can be up to 1 MiB unless an operation documents a lower limit; a larger body returns 413 with the REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE error code.
info.title: Flint Public API

get.description: Returns high-level merchant analytics for the requested half-open period.
Returns merchant payment volume buckets for the requested half-open period.
Returns windowed subscription metrics plus current subscription snapshot metrics.
Returns merchant-bound external API key metadata. Internal keys, demo-session keys, and secrets are never returned. Default order: created_at descending, then api_key_id descending.

post.description: Creates a merchant-bound external API key. A live credential creates a live key, or a test key bound to the sandbox named by sandbox_id. A sandbox-bound credential, such as a test key, creates test keys in its own sandbox only. An onboarding session creates its merchant's first keys here, in its default sandbox. secret_key is returned only in the initial successful response and accepted idempotent replays of the same create request.

get.description: Returns external API key metadata. Secrets, internal keys, and demo-session keys are not returned.

patch.description: Updates an API key's name, access, scopes, or expires_at. Expired keys can be updated, and a future expires_at reactivates one. A revoked key can't be updated. An API key caller may grant only scopes it holds and can manage only keys whose scopes it holds.

post.description: Permanently revokes an external API key and returns metadata with status revoked.

get.description: Returns request summaries, newest first. With developer.request_logs.read the list covers every caller in the credential's environment. With developer.request_logs.self.read it covers only the calling credential's requests. With partner_app_id naming a partner app your merchant owns, the list instead covers that app's partner app token requests in every merchant that installed it, in the credential's mode; the detail route still reads only the credential's environment. Headers, bodies and a reproduction are on the detail route. Default order: created_at descending, then api_request_log_id descending.

x-flint-conditional-scopes.when: Required when filtering by caller_type, caller_id, partner_app_id, or customer_id.

get.description: Returns one request with redacted headers, the redacted request and response bodies for write routes that capture them, and a curl reproduction. Detail older than 14 days has no headers or bodies.

Returns non-secret metadata for the credential that sent the request, as one object per credential type selected by auth_type. API keys, CLI logins, workload identities, partner apps, and onboarding sessions are accepted. No scope is required.

Returns a paginated ledger of balance-affecting transactions, including availability timing and related public resources. Default order: occurred_at descending, then balance_transaction_id descending.
Returns one balance transaction by ID, with optional related order expansion.

Returns the current balance snapshot grouped by currency for the authenticated merchant in the standard list envelope. All balances fit on one page, so next_page_token is omitted. Default order: currency ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.
List bundles. Default order: created_at descending, then bundle_id descending.

post.description: Creates a bundle: several product variants sold as one line at a single price. Send `name` and `unit_price_money`, and list the `components` (variants and quantities). An active bundle needs at least one component, every component must be active, and all components must share the same taxable setting and tax category. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`.

delete.description: Archives a bundle and returns its final state. Returns the archived resource as a read does. Deleting an already archived resource returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references. A stale `expected_version` fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT` and the `current_version`, even when the resource is already archived.

get.description: Returns one bundle by ID, with its price, components, and whether it is available for sale.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a bundle: only the fields you send change. Sending `components` replaces the whole list; omitted components are removed. `expected_version` is required when you send `components` or `images`, and a stale version fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: List bundle components. Default order: position ascending, then bundle_component_id ascending.
List categories. Default order: handle ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Creates a reusable category. If handle is omitted, Flint derives it from the name and never changes it on rename.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an unreferenced category and returns it with status deleted. Deleted categories cannot be retrieved or listed. Remove all product, bundle, promotion, and return configuration references before deleting.

get.description: Returns one category by ID, with its handle, name, and the counts of products and bundles assigned to it. A deleted category fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

patch.description: Updates a category's name, description, `external_reference_id`, or metadata. Only the fields you send change; the handle stays the same. Send `expected_version` to reject the update with `VERSION_CONFLICT` when the category changed since you read it.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of checkout sessions for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then checkout_session_id descending.

post.description: Creates a hosted or headless checkout session for an order, quick-pay charge, subscription plan signup, a return resolution's buyer balance, or what is due now on an invoice. Subscription signup requires a buyer email before payment. Creation never implicitly replaces an open order session. To replace one, send order_id with replace_checkout_session_id set to the expected current session; the compare-and-swap replacement and collection-lock transfer commit atomically. Scopes depend on type: order, quick_pay and subscription_plan need checkouts.checkout_sessions.write, return_resolution needs commerce.returns.resolutions.write, and invoice needs commerce.invoices.write. A credential without the type's scope gets 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE. A return_resolution or invoice session reuses the open session with the same surface and returns 200; a different surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Read the resolution or invoice with its own GET.

get.description: Returns a single checkout session by ID.

patch.description: Updates the mutable fields of a checkout session. A merchant credential can update metadata and external_reference_id, including after the session ends. Send external_reference_id as null to clear it, or metadata as null to clear all metadata. On a session with a subscription_plan_id, either credential can send subscription_terms with the buyer's billing interval and quantity while the session is open and no payment is in progress; a change reprices the signup order and releases the delivery selection. The session's own checkout credential can also send buyer_contact and timezone while the session is open. The buyer_contact field saves the email and phone the buyer entered; send a contact field as null to clear it. The timezone field records the buyer's IANA time zone, which Flint uses for times in the emails it sends the buyer. Saving the same values again changes nothing.

post.description: Closes an open checkout session before it naturally expires.

get.description: Only the session's own checkout credential can read its verification code requests. Only requests whose code hasn't expired are readable until expires_at; an expired, unknown, malformed, deleted, or other session's request returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Emails are masked on every read. A request reads the same whether or not a code was sent, confirmed, or replaced. Reads send nothing and change no code or attempt counters. Returns requests newest first by created_at descending, then checkout_session_customer_verification_id descending. Default order: created_at descending, then checkout_session_customer_verification_id descending.

post.description: Sends a six-digit code to prove the buyer controls an email address or mobile phone number, so this checkout can save a card, use saved details, or confirm a saved card. Only the session's own checkout credential can call it. A retry with the same idempotency key returns the same code request without sending another email or text. See the [headless checkout guide](https://developers.withflintpay.com/docs/guides/headless-checkout) for limits, sandbox codes, SMS copy, and what each answer reveals. To link guest purchases, use POST /v1/customer-verifications.

get.description: Only the session's own checkout credential can read its verification code requests. Only requests whose code hasn't expired are readable until expires_at; an expired, unknown, malformed, deleted, or other session's request returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Emails are masked on every read. A request reads the same whether or not a code was sent, confirmed, or replaced. Reads send nothing and change no code or attempt counters.
get.summary: Get a checkout verification code request

post.description: Checks the code the buyer typed. A right code makes the checkout act for the customer with that email, and creates the customer, with a customer.created event, when none exists. The checkout can then save the buyer's card with save_payment_method on POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay, and list and pay with that customer's saved cards. The order's customer does not change until the payment succeeds. Only the checkout_auth_token in the response acts for that customer. Send it as the Bearer credential from then on. Every other credential for the session, including earlier checkout_auth_token values and hosted checkout links, keeps working for the checkout and acts for no customer, so it lists no saved cards and pays with none. A buyer who opens the link on another device confirms an email there to use them, and from then on only that device's new credential acts for a customer. If the response is lost after the code was accepted, the credential you sent still works. Send the same code again with it while the code is valid, which counts as another try and returns a new credential for the same customer, or request a new code. A wrong, expired, or replaced code fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` and an `INVALID_VALUE` detail on `code`, and so does a used code once the checkout was confirmed again, any code after its 5th try, any code for an email past its limit on wrong tries, or a code whose email's customer changed its email or was deleted after the code was sent. If the checkout stops offering saved payment details before the code is confirmed, such as when the merchant turns them off, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`. A credential that already acts for a customer fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `already_applied`, and confirming never replaces a customer the merchant named. Once the customer whose email the buyer confirmed changes that email or is deleted, the checkout acts for no customer, and the buyer can confirm the customer's new email or another one. A checkout opened from a checkout reminder link acts for no customer the buyer confirmed earlier, so its buyer confirms an email again. A texted code for saved details binds the checkout the same way, but the new credential opens only the cards saved with that number: it lists and pays with no card saved by email, and reads no customer details. A texted code checks once, so after a lost answer request a new code. A code for purpose pay_to_new_address keeps the credential and its proof, omits checkout_auth_token, and refreshes the last confirmed code for 15 minutes. A code for purpose confirm_saved_payment_method keeps the session's credential, so the response omits checkout_auth_token and carries payment_method_save on the checkout session. A texted code saves the card with the number when the number already opens the customer's saved details or the customer has none yet; otherwise payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required turns true, and an emailed code finishes the save. An emailed code alone saves the card by email. After success, a retry with the same idempotency key and code returns the stored answer and credential to any credential of the session. After failure, a retry checks the code again and counts as another try.

get.description: Returns credit notes for the authenticated merchant, newest first. Filter by invoice_id to see everything credited against one invoice. Default order: created_at descending, then credit_note_id descending.

post.description: Creates a draft credit note against an invoice that has been issued and not voided. Include line_items for initial corrections or omit them for an empty draft. The draft uses frozen invoice economics and the remaining pools shared by issued, non-void notes. Drafts reserve no credit. It receives a credit note number when issued.

get.description: Returns one credit note with its lines, total, and the credit still available to allocate.

patch.description: Updates draft credit note fields and corrections atomically. Omitted fields are unchanged, a null memo clears it, and line_items requires expected_version. Replacing lines recalculates their amounts from current remaining creditable pools. Scalar edits preserve stored line values. Issued and void credit notes are frozen.

get.description: Returns every allocation made from a credit note, including reversed ones. Filter by idempotency_key to find the allocation a given request produced. Default order: allocated_at descending, then credit_note_allocation_id descending.

post.description: Applies credit from an issued credit note to its invoice, reducing outstanding_money. The amount cannot exceed the credit note's available_money or the invoice's outstanding balance. Closing the balance with credit sets the invoice to paid when positive net collection remains, or credited when there is no positive net collection. Returns the allocation, the credit note, and the recomputed invoice together. An Idempotency-Key is required and becomes the allocation's identity.

get.description: Returns one allocation. A non-null reversed_at means the credit was returned to the credit note and the invoice balance reopened.

post.description: Reverses an allocation and reopens that much of the invoice balance. The original allocation keeps its row and gains reversed_at, so the history stays append-only. Reversing the allocation that closed an invoice moves it from credited back to open or partially_paid. Reversing credit on a paid invoice that also has collected payments moves it to partially_paid.

Issues a draft credit note and freezes its number, lines, and totals. Provide allocation to issue and apply credit to its invoice atomically, or refund to initiate a linked refund on a paid invoice. Allocation and refund cannot be combined. Omit allocation.amount_money to apply the smaller of the credit available after issue and the invoice's outstanding balance. An explicit amount must be positive, use the invoice's currency, and fit both balances. The result includes credit_note_allocation when allocation is requested. Idempotency-Key is required and is retained for as long as the issue's effects exist, scoped to merchant, environment, credit note, and key. Reuse the key with the identical request to recover the original credit note and allocation. After a lost response, list this note's allocations or refunds filtered by the issue request's idempotency_key. A pending refund is accepted but has not completed. Without allocation or refund, issuance leaves the invoice balance unchanged. Issue validates the stored preview against current shared creditable pools. A fitting correction whose preview changed fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`, which includes the credit note and `current_version`: replace its existing corrections with PATCH using the current expected_version, review the recalculated amounts, and issue again. A stored correction exceeding the remaining pool fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `not_offered`. Update the draft lines before issuing again. Affected historical tax allocations fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `credit_note_tax_reconciliation_required`.

get.description: Returns the credit note document as application/pdf rather than a JSON envelope. The PDF exists from issue onward and shows the credited lines, totals, and the invoice it corrects. It uses your current branding, so a later download can differ in logo or colors, but not in content.

post.description: Voids an issued credit note. Reverse every allocation first. A credit note with a pending or succeeded refund can't be voided. Blockers fail with `RESOURCE_IN_USE`, and `details[0].blocking_resources` lists the allocations and refunds. Void is terminal, and an invoice cannot be voided while an issued credit note stands against it.

get.description: Returns domains ordered by created_at descending, then custom_domain_id descending. Default order: created_at descending, then custom_domain_id descending.

post.description: Configures a checkout or customer account hostname in this environment. Remove an existing hostname of the same type before creating its replacement. If the create response is lost and a retry returns 500 IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, keep the original Idempotency-Key. List domains with GET /v1/custom-domains?type=customer_account and GET /v1/custom-domains?type=customer_account&status=archived, using type=checkout for both requests if that was the original type. Follow pagination and inspect current and archived domains for the requested hostname; use a matching domain's custom_domain_id to retrieve its current state. Do not switch keys or wait for key retention to expire to create again. Contact support with the request_id if the outcome is still unclear.

delete.description: Archives the hostname and starts its redirect retention window. Repeating the request returns the archived domain unchanged.

get.description: Returns a custom domain, including archived domains.

post.description: Starts provider and DNS checks for this domain. Send no body or an empty JSON object. Checks are limited to once every 60 seconds per domain; a request over that limit fails with `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, so wait before validating again.

get.description: Lists deletion requests across the selected merchant environment so a merchant can discover and review buyer-created requests. Default order: requested_at descending, then customer_deletion_request_id descending.

post.description: Creates a deletion request for merchant review, or returns the customer's open request unchanged. No deletion work starts until approval.

get.description: Returns the current status of a tracked deletion request.

post.description: Approves or rejects a pending deletion request. Approval returns processing while account data and buyer credentials are deleted asynchronously. A failed deletion can be approved again but cannot be rejected. Approval is blocked while the customer has non-canceled subscriptions or usable saved payment methods.

Mints a server-side, customer-scoped credential after the merchant has authenticated the buyer. Keep secret and refresh_token on your server. For hosted sign-in, create a customer access link instead.

Rotates a customer session secret and refresh token without a merchant API key. Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the session family. Use one fixed idempotency key per session: Flint scopes the key to the refresh token, so concurrent refreshes replay the same pair. On `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`, retry with the same key and token.
Revokes one customer session in the selected merchant environment. This does not revoke an independent Flint Account buyer session.

get.description: Lists every status for the required customer_id. Status and supported_actions are computed when read. Flint deletes a verification 8 days after its code and proof expire; customer deletion also removes it. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_verification_id descending.

post.description: Sends a Flint verification code to the customer's current email for linking guest purchases. A customer without an email fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. Set purpose to link_guest_purchases; email is the only channel and the default. Confirm the code before linking purchases. Read its current status with GET /v1/customer-verifications/{customer_verification_id}. To prove an email inside a checkout, use POST /v1/checkout-sessions/{checkout_session_id}/customer-verifications.

get.description: Returns one customer verification in any status. Status and supported_actions are computed when read. Flint deletes a verification 8 days after its code and proof expire; customer deletion also removes it.

post.description: Confirms the Flint-sent code and returns a verification that can link guest purchases for its customer. A confirmed verification expires in 15 minutes and can be redeemed once.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of customers for the authenticated merchant. Without a status filter, returns active and deletion_processing customers; deleted customers appear only when the filter names deleted. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_id descending.

post.description: Creates a customer record for a buyer's contact details and purchases in this environment. When an active customer already has `email`, `on_email_conflict` chooses whether to fail with `ALREADY_EXISTS`, which names that customer, or return the existing customer unchanged. Emails match case-insensitively.

get.description: Returns a single customer by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a customer. Clearing email while any subscription is not canceled returns 409 CUSTOMER_EMAIL_REQUIRED. Changing, case-changing, or clearing an existing email requires customer_account.mode to be merchant_hosted; otherwise the update fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`. A customer with no email can be given one in either mode. To change the email of a customer who signs in to your Flint-hosted account, create a customer session for the customer and send POST /v1/me/email-change-requests with the new email; the customer confirms it with the codes Flint emails them. If Flint cannot read the account settings, the update fails with a retryable `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the customer is unchanged.

post.description: Signs the buyer in to your Flint-hosted customer account as this customer. Works for 15 minutes and one open. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. Optionally send return_url for a destination on your site, or omit the body. Requires customers.sessions.write. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this customer's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its open. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

get.description: Lists the customer's saved addresses with billing and shipping default flags. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_address_id descending.

post.description: Creates a stable saved address. The address becomes a default only when the request sets is_default_billing or is_default_shipping, or later by setting those flags with PATCH, including the customer's first address. A saved default becomes the customer's effective address for the corresponding role.

delete.description: Deletes a saved address. Deleting the billing or shipping default leaves the customer with none; Flint doesn't pick another address.

get.description: Returns one saved address owned by the customer.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a saved address. Set is_default_billing or is_default_shipping to true to make this address the default, or false to clear a default it holds. Updating a default address also updates the customer's effective address for that role.

get.description: Returns the preferences for the customer's current email address in this merchant environment. A missing choice is enabled. Reads remain available while deletion is processing. Returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown or deleted customer, or with reason email_missing when the customer has no email address. Merchants cannot change these preferences.

post.description: Links purchases with the verified email and no customer to the verification's customer in the same merchant environment. Purchases bound to another customer stay with that customer. The verification is single use; use the same idempotency key to retry an uncertain result.
post.summary: Link guest purchases to a customer

post.description: Revokes every customer session for one customer in the selected merchant environment. Flint Account buyer sessions remain independent.

get.description: Returns the customer's exemption records ordered by created_at descending, then customer_tax_exemption_id descending. Archived records are excluded by default. Status may filter scheduled, active, expired and archived records, alone or together. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_tax_exemption_id descending.

post.description: Records a nested customer exemption with reason, coverage and an inclusive date window. At most 100 unarchived exemptions may belong to a customer; exceeding that limit returns LIMIT_REACHED with reason customer_tax_exemptions. An active record applies to the customer's sales whose taxable destination its coverage contains, within its date range. Saving a record doesn't change the customer's blanket tax_exempt flag, which still takes precedence. Only API keys and dashboard sessions can access these records. Retry a lost response with the same request and Idempotency-Key. If IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED is returned, inspect this customer's list and GET records before sending a new write. Match a lost create against submitted fields across list pages; contact support with the original key and request ID if its outcome is unclear.

delete.description: Archives the record and returns its archived snapshot in the same schema as GET. It stays readable by ID and is excluded from lists unless status includes archived. Expired and archived records cannot be edited. An optional expected_version query parameter rejects a stale write before effects. Retry a lost response with the same request and Idempotency-Key. If IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED is returned, inspect this customer's list and GET records before sending a new write. Match a lost create against submitted fields across list pages; contact support with the original key and request ID if its outcome is unclear.

get.description: Returns one exemption belonging to this customer, including an archived record. A record belonging to another customer returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Evidence references are merchant-only; customer and checkout sessions cannot access this route.

patch.description: Updates only fields supplied. Coverage is replaced as a whole and requires expected_version. Null clears optional description, certificate_number, evidence_reference and end_date. Metadata merges by key; null values remove individual keys and a null map clears caller-owned metadata. Expired and archived records reject edits with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. A stale expected_version returns VERSION_CONFLICT before effects. Retry a lost response with the same request and Idempotency-Key. If IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED is returned, inspect this customer's list and GET records before sending a new write. Match a lost create against submitted fields across list pages; contact support with the original key and request ID if its outcome is unclear.

get.description: Returns delivery location sets in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_location_set_id ascending.

post.description: Delivery location sets pin reusable sets of Locations for allocation or buyer pickup. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. It starts active.

delete.description: Retires the delivery location set. An active delivery method whose current revision still uses the location set as its origin blocks deletion: the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking methods. Point those methods at another origin first. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects.

get.description: Returns the current revision and lifecycle state for one delivery location set.

patch.description: Sparsely updates mutable fields. A request that carries configuration publishes a new immutable revision, even when its values are unchanged, and requires expected_version. Other fields advance version and keep the current revision. Archived resources can't be changed; create a new resource instead.

get.description: Returns delivery methods in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_method_id ascending.

post.description: Delivery methods combine eligibility, pricing, schedules, estimates, tax treatment, and execution behavior. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. Omit status to start inactive.

delete.description: Retires the delivery method after checking current dependencies. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects. A method referenced by checkout.default_delivery_method_ids at merchant scope or by delivery_method_ids on an active or inactive payment link cannot be archived; the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking references. Remove the method from checkout.default_delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/settings or from the link's delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/payment-links/{payment_link_id}. Open checkout sessions keep their pinned revision and do not block retirement.

get.description: Returns the current revision and lifecycle state for one delivery method.

patch.description: Sparsely updates mutable fields. A request that carries configuration, name, description, display_position, or recommendation_priority publishes a new immutable revision, even when its values are unchanged, and requires expected_version. Other fields, such as status, metadata, and external_reference_id, advance version and keep the current revision, so they never replace a revoked revision. Archived resources can't be changed; create a new resource instead. A method referenced by checkout.default_delivery_method_ids at merchant scope or by delivery_method_ids on an active or inactive payment link cannot be set inactive; the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking references. Remove the method from checkout.default_delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/settings or from the link's delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/payment-links/{payment_link_id}.

post.description: Computes delivery options with mode delivery_options or up to 25 pickup locations with mode pickup_locations. Creates no resource, holds no inventory, and does not change the current selection. Pickup locations are nearest first when a buyer location is provided. Merchant callers receive diagnostics. Checkout credentials may use only pickup_locations for their own checkout session.

get.description: Returns delivery profiles in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_profile_id ascending.

post.description: Delivery profiles define reusable delivery rules assigned to catalog obligations. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. It starts active.

delete.description: Retires the delivery profile. Product variants, bundle components, or a catalog default that still use the profile block deletion: the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking references. Assign those items to another delivery profile first. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects.

get.description: Returns the current revision and lifecycle state for one delivery profile.

patch.description: Sparsely updates mutable fields. Send is_default true to make this active profile the physical catalog default, together with any other mutable fields in one atomic update. Sending only is_default true for the current default leaves its version unchanged and emits no events. A request that carries configuration publishes a new immutable revision, even when its values are unchanged, and requires expected_version. Other fields advance version and keep the current revision. Archived resources can't be changed; create a new resource instead.

post.description: Assigns this active delivery profile to physical product variants and bundle components that don't have one. Flint accepts the request with `202`, then assigns the profile in batches after responding. To know when it's done, poll `GET /v1/delivery-profiles/{delivery_profile_id}`, waiting at least `Retry-After` seconds between reads, until `unconfigured_assignment.status` is `completed`, `canceled`, or `failed`. Each item keeps `delivery_configuration_status` `action_required` until its batch commits, and each batch sends the `updated` events of the variants, products, and bundles it changes. An item that gets a profile from another write first keeps it. A newer assignment takes over from one still running, and the earlier one becomes `canceled` with `cancellation_reason` `superseded`. If the profile is archived before the assignment finishes, it becomes `canceled` with `cancellation_reason` `delivery_profile_archived` and the remaining items stay unconfigured.

get.description: Returns delivery quotes with status derived identically to individual quote reads. A checkout credential must send its own checkout_session_id and receives the buyer view. Quotes are ordered by created_at and delivery_quote_id ascending. Each page scans at most 500 rows and may contain fewer than page_size items while next_page_token is present. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_quote_id ascending.

post.description: Creates an exact delivery quote for the checkout session named by checkout_session_id, without holding inventory. A checkout credential can quote only its own checkout session.

get.description: Returns a delivery quote by its ID. API keys receive the same merchant view as the quote list. A checkout credential reads only quotes of its own checkout session and receives the buyer view; any other quote is refused as not found.
Returns delivery rate callbacks in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_rate_callback_id ascending.

post.description: Delivery callback endpoints pin shared outbound callback transport configuration. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. signing_methods defaults to ["jwt"]. JWTs use Flint's public JWKS and this callback's delivery_rate_callback_id as aud. Verify body_sha256 against the exact request bytes. The jwt method sends Authorization: Bearer, and the hmac method sends webhook-signature and Flint-Signing-Key-Ids. Every request includes webhook-id and webhook-timestamp. When hmac is included, the response returns the shared secret and its delivery_rate_callback_signing_key_id once; no later response returns them. It starts inactive.

delete.description: Retires the delivery rate callback. An active delivery method whose current revision still prices with the rate callback blocks deletion: the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking methods. Move those methods to another pricing strategy first. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects.

get.description: Returns the current revision and lifecycle state for one delivery rate callback.

patch.description: Sparsely updates mutable fields. A request that carries configuration or signing_methods publishes a new immutable revision, even when its values are unchanged, and requires expected_version. Other fields, such as name, external_reference_id, and status, advance version and keep the current revision, so they never replace a revoked revision. signing_methods replaces the set. Adding hmac when the callback has no shared secret issues one and returns it once, with its delivery_rate_callback_signing_key_id, in this response. Removing hmac deletes all shared secrets. Archived resources can't be changed; create a new resource instead.

post.description: Sends a minimal signed probe to verify endpoint reachability and callback credentials without running a synthetic rate evaluation. The Idempotency-Key fingerprint includes the delivery_rate_callback_id path value and request body. A retry replays the original result even after the callback changes or is archived.

Replaces the callback's shared secret and returns the callback with the new secret and its delivery_rate_callback_signing_key_id once. Flint signs with both keys for one hour. A callback without hmac returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued; PATCH signing_methods to include hmac to issue the first secret.

Sends a signed delivery rate callback with synthetic non-PII data and returns a safe result. The Idempotency-Key fingerprint includes the delivery_rate_callback_id path value and request body. A retry replays the original result even after the callback changes or is archived.

get.description: Returns permanent delivery revocations, newest first by created_at and delivery_revocation_id. Default order: created_at descending, then delivery_revocation_id descending.

post.description: Permanently fences one exact delivery method revision, rate callback revision, callback HMAC signing key, or recorded Location geography version. Name both the parent and the exact child. Unknown targets return RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND without effects; a duplicate returns ALREADY_EXISTS with the existing revocation. Issued quotes are revoked immediately. Provisional selections are released before they can be used again.

get.description: Returns one permanent delivery revocation and its estimated impact at creation time.

Returns a checkout session's or an order's delivery selections, current and earlier, newest first by created_at and delivery_selection_id, with economics, lifecycle events, and retention-aware private data. Send checkout_session_id or order_id. A checkout credential must send its own checkout_session_id. With a status filter, each page examines at most 500 selections and may hold fewer than page_size while next_page_token is present. Default order: created_at descending, then delivery_selection_id descending.

post.description: Selects one unexpired option per required choice group of delivery_quote_id. Replaces the checkout's provisional selection and stock hold, applies delivery charges, and returns the repriced order. Shipment and local delivery choices can keep a partial quote address when destination_address is omitted. Missing destination members and recipient fields appear in input_requirements and must be supplied by replacing the selection before payment. The selection acts on the quote's checkout session. A checkout credential can select only from quotes of its own checkout session; any other quote is refused as not found.

get.description: Returns one delivery selection, current or earlier, with its economics, lifecycle events, and retention-aware private data. While the selection is selected, the tax on its delivery charges follows the order's tax. A checkout credential reads only its own session's selections and receives the buyer view; any other selection is refused as not found.

post.description: Clears the checkout's provisional selection: releases its stock hold, removes its delivery charges, and recalculates the order. Available while supported_actions lists release. A checkout credential can release only its own session's selection; any other is refused as not found.

get.description: Returns delivery zones in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_zone_id ascending.

post.description: Delivery zones define versioned geographic eligibility. Creation publishes immutable revision 1. It starts active.

delete.description: Retires the delivery zone. An active delivery method whose current revision still uses the zone blocks deletion: the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking methods. Remove the zone from those methods first. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects.

get.description: Returns the current revision and lifecycle state for one delivery zone.

patch.description: Sparsely updates mutable fields. A request that carries configuration publishes a new immutable revision, even when its values are unchanged, and requires expected_version. Other fields advance version and keep the current revision. Archived resources can't be changed; create a new resource instead.

post.description: Creates a temporary demo sandbox and returns a short-lived test API key. The secret key is displayed only at creation time and for a short idempotent retry window. Omit template to use quickstart; an explicit empty or unsupported value is invalid.

Ends the active or provisioning demo session identified by demo_session_id for this client and provisions a fresh one. A client that lost its create response gets the current session ID from current_resource.resource_id on ALREADY_EXISTS. A retry with the same idempotency key and body replays the replacement before checking the current session, including its secret during the secret delivery window. After that window, the retry returns ALREADY_EXISTS with the current session reference. The daily cap applies only to fresh executions. Omit template to use quickstart; an explicit empty or unsupported value is invalid.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of devices for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then device_id descending.

post.description: Creates a device. If an active device already has the hardware_fingerprint, fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS` and reason `hardware_fingerprint_already_exists`, and changes nothing. The details[0].current_resource field names the existing device.

delete.description: Archives a device and releases its hardware_fingerprint for reuse. The archived device no longer returns hardware_fingerprint. A device that an active reader names returns `409 RESOURCE_IN_USE` with those readers in `blocking_resources`: archive them or clear their `device_id` first.

get.description: Returns a single device by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a device. Send null to clear location_id or all metadata. The name field cannot be null. Archived devices return ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason archived and current_status archived.

post.description: Evaluates promotion outcomes for an order without changing it. Returns the complete result inside data, without creating a resource or requiring an idempotency key. Use `promotion_id` for server-side apply flows where you already know the promotion, including code-gated promotions, which then apply without a code and count only toward the promotion's `max_uses`. Checkout credentials must use `promotion_code`. The response includes applied, skipped, and single-threshold available promotion candidates.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of disputes for the authenticated merchant with optional payment, customer, status, reason, case type, action required, and timing filters. Defaults to created_at descending. The amount sort compares amount_money.amount in minor units. The evidence_due_at sort places disputes without deadlines last in either direction. Default order: created_at descending, then dispute_id descending.
Returns one dispute by ID, with optional customer, order, and payment intent expansions.

post.description: Accepts a chargeback: you won't contest it, and the disputed amount stays with the buyer. The dispute becomes `lost`, and Flint sends `dispute.lost`. You can accept while `status` is `needs_response` and `is_action_required` is `true`. An inquiry can't be accepted; refund the payment or respond with evidence instead. Accepting can't be undone. Requires `payments.disputes.write`. Send no body or `{}`. If you don't receive a response, retry with the same idempotency key, or read the dispute: `status: lost` means it was accepted.

Creates a browser session for responding to or viewing a dispute with Stripe Connect. Requires payments.disputes.write. Allowed for closed disputes; bank returns cannot be contested. Pass the returned payment to setPayment or the React payment prop. Each completed retry creates a fresh single-use client secret. Keep your API key on your server.

Sandbox only. Simulates the card network's ruling on a dispute that needs a response. Flint submits Stripe's test evidence for the `outcome`, and the ruling arrives through the dispute's usual webhook events, as a real one would. Send `won` or `lost` for a chargeback in `needs_response`, and `inquiry_closed` or `escalated` for an inquiry in `inquiry_needs_response`. The response is the dispute after the evidence is submitted, usually `under_review` or `inquiry_under_review`. Stripe decides shortly after, with no fixed timing. Requires `payments.disputes.write`. If you don't receive a response, retry with the same idempotency key, or read the dispute.
Reads an emailed preference token without signing the buyer in. The merchant key must match the token's merchant and environment. Tokens belong in the request body and must stay on your backend.
post.summary: Look up an email preference link

post.description: Disables the email preference represented by an emailed token without signing the buyer in. Repeating the request keeps it disabled. The merchant key must match the token's merchant and environment.

Reads an address's email preferences without putting it in a URL. Matches after trimming surrounding whitespace and ignoring case. Returns the same shape as the customer preference read. For an address without a current customer, customer_id and version are null. With multiple matching customers, returns the first customer in ID order. A category with no stored choice is enabled. Merchants cannot change these preferences.

get.description: Lists feedback reports in descending creation order for the credential's merchant and environment. Default order: created_at descending, then feedback_report_id descending.

post.description: Stores one immutable occurrence of Flint feedback. Use one report per root cause and include only the evidence needed to describe Flint's behavior.

get.description: Returns one immutable feedback report in the credential's merchant and environment.

post.description: Upload a local image to Flint. Create a file, PUT the bytes to upload.url with upload.method and every upload.headers value, then POST /v1/files/{file_id}/complete. The URL works for 15 minutes. Purpose requires its own write scope: product and product_variant use commerce.products.write; bundle uses commerce.bundles.write; payment_link uses checkouts.payment_links.write; subscription_plan uses commerce.subscription_plans.write; merchant_logo and merchant_icon use merchants.profile.write. Logo and icon files are merchant-wide. Creating or completing them requires a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session in any selected environment; test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`. All other purposes belong to the authenticated environment. Partner install tokens need the same purpose scope; a live install token with merchants.profile.write can upload merchant_logo and merchant_icon. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, and route. A replay returns the original upload target without extending its expiry. After a lost response, retry with the same idempotency key or create another file. Each upload URL expires 15 minutes after creation.

get.description: Returns a file's current status without upload credentials. Purpose requires its own read scope: product and product_variant use commerce.products.read; bundle uses commerce.bundles.read; payment_link uses checkouts.payment_links.read; subscription_plan uses commerce.subscription_plans.read; merchant_logo and merchant_icon use merchants.profile.read. The matching write scope also grants read access. Dashboard sessions require the purpose's manage capability. Logo and icon files are merchant-wide; other files belong to the authenticated environment. Partner install tokens need the same purpose scope. Expired deadlines are reflected immediately. Only ready files include url, width, and height. The response uses Cache-Control: no-store.

post.description: Completing a merchant_logo or merchant_icon file requires a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session in any selected environment. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`. After PUT succeeds, complete the file to process its image. Returns the ready file; completing a ready file again returns it. Send no request body or {}. Completing before the bytes arrive returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason status_not_reached and current_status awaiting_upload. Attach the returned file_id as images[].file_id before expires_at, 24 hours after processing. Completion requires the purpose's write scope, with the same merchant-wide branding and environment boundaries as createFile. Partner install tokens need the same purpose scope; a live install token with merchants.profile.write can upload merchant_logo and merchant_icon. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, route, and file_id. A replay returns the original result; it does not extend upload or attachment deadlines. After a lost completion response, repeat this route with the same key and file_id.

get.description: Lists early fraud warnings that card networks reported on your payments, most recently reported first. Filter with `is_actionable=true` to find warnings a full refund can still resolve before a dispute. Default order: reported_at descending, then fraud_warning_id descending.
Retrieves an early fraud warning. Expand `payment_intent` or `dispute` to include them.
Lists provider-neutral fulfillment events. sort_direction applies to both the selected timestamp and the ID tiebreaker. Default order: received_at descending, then fulfillment_event_id descending.

post.description: Records an observational event for a fulfillment or one of its shipments or packages. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Retrieves one provider-neutral fulfillment event by ID.
Returns persisted fulfillment notification audit records. Results default to newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then fulfillment_notification_id descending.
Retrieves one fulfillment notification audit record by ID.

Returns a paginated list of fulfillments. scheduled_start_at uses the service scheduled start or the start of the pickup, local delivery, or shipment window. For scheduled_start_at and terminal_at, null values sort first ascending and last descending. Default order: created_at descending, then fulfillment_id descending.

post.description: Creates a fulfillment for the specified quantities on a paid order. Idempotency-Key is required for every request because an inline shipped package can consume inventory. Save the key before sending and retry the same key and body after a lost response. GET /v1/fulfillments supports order_id and external_reference_id filters, but not idempotency_key; an empty list does not prove creation failed. If replay cannot recover the result, contact support with the original key and request ID instead of creating another fulfillment. A line that does not require fulfillment returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST with detail code NOT_ALLOWED at line_items[i].order_line_item_id; an unknown line ID returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Use this when you manage fulfillment outside checkout; checkout creates fulfillments for the buyer's delivery selections. While Flint is creating those fulfillments, requests for their quantities return OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS with reason delivery_selection_materializing. Retrieve the order and use its fulfillments. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached` when the order is not paid. See the [fulfillment guide](/docs/guides/fulfillment).

get.description: Retrieves a single fulfillment by ID.

patch.description: Updates mutable fulfillment fields and fulfillment-specific details. Fulfillment line item allocation is set when the fulfillment is created. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied.

post.description: Accepts pending fulfillment work so preparation can begin. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Cancels fulfillment work that has not completed. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Completes the fulfillment and records its completion time. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records that a shipment or local delivery fulfillment has left for its destination. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records fulfillment failure and explicitly releases or preserves the allocated quantities. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Pauses fulfillment work with a required merchant hold reason. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records a missed service appointment with a required no-show reason. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records that the items for a shipment fulfillment have been packed. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records that the items for a shipment fulfillment have been picked. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records that preparation of a pickup or delivery fulfillment has begun. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Records that a pickup is ready for collection or a delivery is ready for dispatch. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Releases a merchant hold and restores the previous fulfillment status. An active payment hold must lift first. Schedules and progress timestamps are preserved and no buyer notification is sent. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Sets the start and end of a service fulfillment's appointment window. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Starts fulfillment work. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Lists funding dispositions in descending ID order within the authenticated merchant and environment. Filter by idempotency_key to recover a committed command. Default order: gift_card_funding_disposition_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Accepts a confirmed funding dispute loss and honors all gift card value funded by that payment, including value restored to replacement cards. Records the dispute amount, original gift card consideration, honored value and preserved reservations. Clears only this dispute restriction; balances, unrelated restrictions and unresolved payment reservations remain intact. Requires gift card adjustment authority and a durable idempotency key.
post.summary: Create a gift card funding disposition

get.description: Retrieves a committed funding disposition within the authenticated merchant and environment.
get.summary: Get a gift card funding disposition

get.description: Lists funding lots in descending ID order. Consideration may be null for imported balances whose original purchase price is unknown. The idempotency_key filter recovers a load after a lost command response. Default order: gift_card_load_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Adds positive value with separately recorded consideration and funding provenance. Limits apply to externally funded value and imports as well as Flint-funded sales. Loading a pending card activates it; loading a frozen card does not remove its restrictions. expected_gift_card_version fences the gift card version.
