A set that is still attached to a product, variant, or bundle fails with `RESOURCE_IN_USE`; set `modifier_set_id` to `null` on each of them first. Returns the archived resource as a read does. Deleting an already archived resource returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references. A stale `expected_version` fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT` and the `current_version`, even when the resource is already archived.

get.description: Returns one modifier set by ID, with its ordered modifier groups.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a modifier set: only the fields you send change. Sending `modifier_groups` replaces the set's group entries; entries you leave out are removed, and `expected_version` is required with it. A stale version fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: Starts a partner app install in the merchant's browser. Flint validates the request, then redirects to Flint's consent screen, where the merchant signs in, chooses a merchant, and approves or denies the requested permissions. Flint then redirects to redirect_uri with code, state, and mode, or with an OAuth error. Request errors found before consent also redirect with an OAuth error once client_id and redirect_uri are validated. Unknown or inactive clients and missing or unregistered redirect URIs return the Flint error envelope. This route takes no credential, and Flint ignores any Authorization header. Flint ignores unrecognized parameters.

Validates the install link inputs and returns the partner app metadata and requested permissions for the consent screen. This route takes no credential, and Flint ignores a single Authorization header, as GET /v1/oauth/authorize does. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization. Flint ignores unrecognized parameters.

post.description: First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Authenticates the current refresh token without consuming or rotating it. Returns only currently authorized contexts, including an empty list. Listing does not change consent, revoke contexts, or update session state. Read approved scopes from the selected context's token response or /v1/auth-context. No business access is granted. Default order: the order of the contexts approved at the latest consent.

First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Send session_mode=contexts for a session that supports additive reauthorization. The required scope field contains the full requested set as space-separated names. Login sends the scopes it needs, and login with extra permissions sends those plus the additions. No scopes are implicitly added. The browser may approve a subset per context; token scope reports the approved set. Unknown scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope. Selected scopes are checked against the selected merchant and environment before approval.

First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Starts device consent bound to the current session and user without consuming the refresh token. Without scope_mode, approval replaces consent; denial or expiry leaves consent unchanged. Redeem using the device_code grant to rotate the latest family token. Set scope_mode=additive and context_id to request additional space-separated scope names for one existing context. Merchant and environment are derived from that context; conflicting hints return invalid_context. Approval unions only browser-approved additions with that context's existing scopes and preserves all other contexts. No implicit bootstrap scopes are added. Unsupported or environment-disallowed scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope; browser denial returns access_denied when polling. Partial approval succeeds and scope in the token response is authoritative. A superseded consent review returns expired_token when its device code is redeemed; start a new review. The existing session remains active.

RFC 7009 token revocation for partner apps and flint-cli. Partner apps authenticate with client assertions, HTTP Basic, or client_secret. Assertion rules match the token endpoint. Self-signed private_key_jwt assertions (iss=sub=client_id; ES256, ES384, PS256, RS256, or EdDSA; a single-use jti; exp at most five minutes ahead) are verified against public_key or jwks_url credentials, so sign a fresh one with a new jti for each request. Workload identity assertions have the external issuer as iss and are verified with that issuer's published keys; they use RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, or ES512, expire no more than one hour and 60 seconds ahead, and need no jti. Revoking a partner app token ends that token only; token_type_hint is only a hint. Unknown, expired, and other clients' tokens return 200 with no change. Revoking a token never changes an install or grant.

For flint-cli, revoking an access or refresh token ends its CLI session and invalidates the session's tokens. The public client sends client_id=flint-cli without a secret or Authorization header. Send application/x-www-form-urlencoded; success has an empty body. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope.

Partner apps authenticate with client assertions, HTTP Basic, or client_secret_post. Assertions require client_id, client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer, and client_assertion; never mix them with a secret or HTTP Basic. Self-signed private_key_jwt assertions are verified against the app's public_key and jwks_url credentials. They require iss=sub=client_id, a single-string aud equal to the Flint issuer, exp no more than five minutes ahead, and a single-use jti, signed with ES256, ES384, PS256, RS256 (RSA keys of 2048 to 4096 bits and exponent 65537), or EdDSA. Workload identity assertions are tokens from the external issuer of a workload_identity credential: iss is that issuer, and Flint verifies them with the issuer's published keys. They must match the credential's subject, audience, and claim conditions, be signed with RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, or ES512, and expire no more than one hour and 60 seconds ahead; Flint does not require a jti. Assertion replay storage outages, and JWKS URL or issuer outages that leave no usable keys, return 503 temporarily_unavailable. Partner apps get partner app tokens: opaque fpat_ Bearer tokens for one mode that last 900 seconds, with no refresh token. grant_type=client_credentials mints one with the app's client authentication; mode (test or live) is required, and merchant_id optionally binds the token to one merchant, checked for format only. scope is refused with invalid_scope, because each request uses the selected merchant's grant. Only server apps can mint, and a partner client that sends grant_type=refresh_token gets unauthorized_client. The response has access_token, token_type, expires_in, partner_app_id, mode, and merchant_id for a merchant-bound token. Each app can mint 600 tokens per minute after client authentication, beside the per-IP budget; over it returns HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason: resource. Cache one token per mode and mint again when it expires. grant_type=authorization_code exchanges a 5-minute, single-use code with S256 PKCE, activates the install and environment grant, and returns a partner app token bound to the installing merchant and the grant's mode, with scope (the granted permission IDs), merchant_id, partner_app_install_id, environment_grant_id, mode, and sandbox_id in test mode. Reusing a code returns invalid_grant and revokes the token its first exchange minted; the grant stays. Deleting the credential that minted a token, disabling the client secret, rotating it with an immediate expiry, and archiving the app revoke the affected tokens. This endpoint follows OAuth token endpoint conventions: send application/x-www-form-urlencoded only. Failures return OAuth token error objects. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope before client authentication.

The public client flint-cli supports the RFC 8628 device_code grant and rotating refresh tokens. Pending device requests return authorization_pending; early polling returns slow_down and increases the required interval by five seconds; denial returns access_denied; expired or consumed codes return expired_token. CLI access tokens last 15 minutes. CLI sessions expire after 30 days idle or 90 days total. Reusing a rotated CLI refresh token revokes its family, including when the previous response was lost. A fresh browser login is then required.

With session_mode=contexts at CLI authorization, tokens include oauth_session_id and context_id. CLI refresh requires an explicitly authorized context_id; invalid_context and context_access_denied do not consume the refresh token. Each CLI access token is limited to one context. Ordinary CLI rotation preserves other unexpired access tokens; removing consent immediately invalidates affected tokens. CLI refresh scope may request a subset of the selected grant or context scopes. Only the issued access token is narrowed; consent and other tokens are unchanged. A later refresh without scope restores the full consented scopes. Legacy CLI sessions retain their original response shape. Request rate limits return HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. Device-code token polling returns HTTP 400 slow_down for both early polls and request rate limits.

Workload identities use grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange with subject_token, subject_token_type, and workload_identity_id. subject_token_type must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt or urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Optional scope narrows the identity scopes for this token; requested_token_type, if supplied, must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. Client authentication, client_id, actor_token, resource, audience, and unrecognized fields are forbidden and return invalid_request. The response includes an opaque fwat_ access token, issued_token_type, workload_identity_id, merchant_id, mode, and sandbox_id in test mode, without a refresh token. The token expires after the shorter of one hour and the remaining subject-token lifetime. Identity deactivation, archive, and scope narrowing take effect on the next API request. Exchange errors use invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_scope, unsupported_grant_type, temporarily_unavailable, and server_error. Limits are 300 requests per minute per IP and 600 per minute per identity after signature verification; exceeding either returns HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. No usable external issuer keys returns HTTP 503 temporarily_unavailable.

Creates a link into Flint-hosted onboarding for the authenticated merchant environment, for products that don't embed Connect.js. The page opens Account Onboarding and Notification Banner in the credential's mode, names the business, and for a partner app install token names the app. The link opens once, within 5 minutes, into a browser session of at most an hour, and every refresh of the page rechecks the credential that created it: revoking the API key, CLI login, or install, or authorizing the app again, ends the page. When the person exits or finishes, or opens a used or expired link, the page offers one action: back to return_url. The url is a bearer credential that lets whoever opens it enter identity and bank details for the merchant. Create it only for a person you just authenticated and authorized for this merchant, redirect them to it at once, and never email or log it. Takes the credentials of POST /v1/merchant-account-sessions. A partner app install token works in live mode only while its app's merchant_onboarding platform capability is active; otherwise it gets 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with the reason its platform status gives: platform_onboarding_required, platform_pending_review, platform_rejected, or platform_capability_inactive. A same-key, same-input retry replays the original link for 24 hours without extending its lifetime or replenishing its open. Use a new key for a new link.

Submits whatever the caller currently knows, re-evaluates onboarding, reconciles onboarding requirements, and returns the next step in the consolidated onboarding state machine. Send an empty JSON object when the current next_step only asks to refresh onboarding requirements. The credential selects the environment; the onboarding session token acts in the merchant's default sandbox. A partner install token can't send profile.email, and in live mode works only while its app's merchant_onboarding platform capability is active; otherwise it gets 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with the reason its platform status gives: platform_onboarding_required, platform_pending_review, platform_rejected, or platform_capability_inactive.
Starts the consolidated onboarding flow by accepting a verification email for asynchronous delivery and returning a temporary verification token. Success does not confirm email delivery.

get.description: Returns the consolidated onboarding state machine, including the primary next step for agents or humans. This endpoint is read-only. The credential selects the environment; the onboarding session token acts in the merchant's default sandbox.

post.description: Verifies the emailed code, provisions the Flint user and merchant if needed, and returns an onboarding session token. The token expires at onboarding_session_expires_at and cannot be refreshed. Verify the email again to get a new one. Read GET /v1/onboarding/state next.

get.description: Returns the Flint public OpenAPI document for tooling, schema inspection, and client generation. The document describes one API version: the `version` query parameter if you send it, otherwise the `Flint-Version` header, otherwise Flint's current version. The route takes no credential. The body is gzip-compressed when the request's `Accept-Encoding` header accepts gzip.

post.description: Calculates removing items from a paid order, adding items to it, or both, without changing it. Only whole unassigned units are removable; bundle components must all be unassigned. Original line quantity and pricing stay unchanged. Each removed unit's value includes its share of discounts and tax. Charges are released only when you list them in charge_refunds. Added lines use the line item create shape, are priced and taxed as usual without promotions, and must be lines Flint can fulfill: variant, bundle, and custom lines with a delivery requirement. The removed value and released charges pay for added lines first, removals in request order and then charges; the rest is refund_money, and what the added lines cost beyond that is amount_due_money. Invoice-collected, subscription-owned, return-owned, and disputed orders, and orders with an unresolved inventory exception, cannot be edited. Refund a line without fulfillment quantities, such as a digital item or service, with POST /v1/refunds. This calculation holds no stock and sets aside no refundable amount.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of orders for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then order_id descending.

post.description: Creates an order for the authenticated merchant. For USD orders, an effective requested tip may be up to the larger of $1,000 or 100% of the post-discount merchandise subtotal.

get.description: Returns a single order by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to mutable order fields such as customer_id, notes, metadata, tax, the delivery destination, and the requested tip. catalog_price_behavior defaults to keep. Send reprice with an explicit non-null customer_id to refresh every catalog variant line on an open, unpaid order; reassignment resolves the new customer’s direct list, then segment list, then variant prices. Customer removal is not supported. Checkout verification never reprices existing lines. A request containing only metadata, internal_note, buyer_note, or external_reference_id, with optional expected_version, can update open, closed, paid, and invoice-locked orders without changing totals. Other merchant edits keep hosted and headless checkout sessions open unless an edit closes or completes the order, which ends the session with order_mutated. Edits can also end invoice, return-resolution, and subscription-plan sessions with order_mutated. A session already past expires_at ends with expired before the edit is applied. These annotation updates are blocked while any order payment attempt remains non-terminal, including an authorization awaiting capture, or checkout payment work is still resolving. Requests combining annotations with other fields use the financial mutation rules for the entire request. Send requested_tip: null to clear the current requested tip. Once a payment's capture sets its own tip with tip_money, the order's tip is set per payment: setting or clearing requested_tip returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason payment_collected. A merchant can correct a paid subscription signup or renewal destination before shipment by sending delivery_destination and the current order version as expected_version. The committed delivery methods must remain eligible, and shipping and tax totals must stay unchanged. When the correction would change the paid totals, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `payment_collected`. The detail can include shipping_money, requoted_shipping_money, tax_money, and requoted_tax_money.

x-flint-conditional-scopes.when: Required when delivery is present, including null.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's receipt email carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in, and lets the buyer have the receipt sent again to the order's email. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the order. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`, and for an order without a customer, with reason `configuration_required`. Dashboard sessions may create links when the staff member can view orders. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

get.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource. Default order: created_at descending, then order_activity_id descending.
Returns the order's charges sorted by ID in ascending order. Default order: order_charge_id ascending.

post.description: Adds a service charge, fee, or surcharge to an order.

delete.description: Removes a single service charge, fee, or surcharge from an order.

patch.description: Updates a single service charge, fee, or surcharge on an order.

post.description: Closes an open order and stops further payment. Cancels pending discounts, releases their reservations, and recalculates totals; canceled discounts remain visible with status: "canceled" but no longer reduce the total. Unused order-owned payment intents are canceled. When collected money remains refundable, send collected_money_behavior: keep to close and keep it, or refund it first with POST /v1/refunds and order_id. Closing does not refund money; refunds remain available afterwards. Closing is blocked while payment collection is in progress. To complete a zero-balance order as paid, use POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay. closed_reason and closed_at record why and when the order closed. The request body is optional. Send expected_version to reject a mutation based on an outdated order read.
Applies a promotion-backed or manual discount to an order. Checkout-authenticated buyers must provide a promotion code; resource IDs and manual discounts require merchant authentication.

Removes pending applied discounts or deferred promotions from an order. Send at least one ID across order_discount_ids and deferred_promotion_ids. Deferred promotions can be removed before payment. Redeemed or canceled discounts are settlement history and cannot be removed.
Recalculates pending discounts and automatic promotions for a mutable order. The request body is optional. Send expected_version to reject a mutation based on an outdated order read.

get.description: Lists immutable edits for this order, newest created_at first, with descending order_edit_id as the tiebreaker. Defaults to 20 results. Keep filters unchanged when using a page token. Default order: created_at descending, then order_edit_id descending.

post.description: Removes unassigned units from a paid order, adds items the removed value and released charges pay for, or does both, and queues any remaining refund atomically. Removed value and released charges pay for added lines first; only the remainder is refunded. Added lines are priced and taxed as usual, without promotions, and must be variant, bundle, or custom lines with a delivery requirement. They do not join the order's delivery selection. An edit that would leave a balance due writes nothing and returns LIMIT_EXCEEDED with reason order_edit_balance_due, with maximum_money equal to the removed value plus released charges. Bundle components must all be unassigned; dispatched quantities use Returns. Original quantities and pricing remain the sale record. The edit, added stock commitments, committed tax, and release of removed stock commit together; refund processing can continue afterward. Invoice-collected, subscription-owned, return-owned, disputed orders and unresolved inventory exceptions cannot be edited. Charges change only through charge_refunds. A zero-value edit creates no refund. Refund processing may still be pending, so refunds can be empty and refund.created follows later. Refund failures leave this immutable edit recorded. When supported_actions contains retry, use POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/edits/{order_edit_id}/retry to refund the remaining money. On VERSION_CONFLICT, keep the draft, fetch the order, preview again, and reconcile it before committing with the new expected_order_version and a new key. Retry a lost response with the original Idempotency-Key and unchanged body: Flint recovers the committed edit and its current order and refunds, without repeating the edit. If recovery cannot complete, retain the key and request ID for support; do not change keys to retry an uncertain result.

get.description: Returns an immutable edit with its frozen refund amounts and current refund IDs. The internal note is visible to merchant callers only.

post.description: Refunds the edit's remaining frozen money after refund processing has failed. Pending and succeeded linked refunds count toward the edit's refunded value. Omit the body or destinations to reuse the edit's original destinations. Retry is unavailable while a linked refund is pending, when nothing remains, or when a payment is disputed. While Flint is still processing the original refund and no linked refund exists, supported_actions is empty and retry returns in_progress. If processing ends without creating a refund, retry becomes available. Use a new Idempotency-Key for a new retry attempt, and the same key and body to recover its lost response. The response contains only refunds created by this attempt.

Selects a gift card by its current code and returns masked selections and an unreserved estimate. No value is held or debited. Optional expected_version must match the order version returned by the last read. An order may select at most 20 gift cards. Gift card value cannot pay for subscription orders. Retry a lost response with the same idempotency key to recover the original selection result.
post.summary: Apply a gift card to an order

delete.description: Removes a selected gift card without moving value. The expected_version must still match the order version. Selections cannot change during an active payment attempt. Retry a lost response with the same idempotency key to recover the original selection result.

get.description: Returns the order's line items sorted by ID in ascending order. Default order: order_line_item_id ascending.

post.description: Adds one or more line items to an order.

delete.description: Removes a single line item from an order.

patch.description: Updates a single line item on an order. On paid orders, send expected_ship_date as a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date or null to clear it. It must be the only field apart from expected_version. expected_version is the order version returned in data.version. Send gift_card_face_value_money and expected_version to select an unpaid gift card line's face value within its frozen offer and reprice the order before any purchase funding. Send gift_card_recipient and expected_version to replace or clear recipient delivery details before any purchase funding. Checkout credentials can update gift card face value and recipient details together, modifiers, or a line subscription offer selection, each with expected_version. Repeating the current gift card face value does not change the order version. Set subscription to null to buy the line once.

post.description: Starts or resumes a payment attempt on the order. Starting a subscription requires buyer_contact.email or an email already saved on the checkout session or order. Set action to pay to charge the full outstanding balance, confirm_payment_intents to confirm order-owned payment intents, setup to save a newly collected token on a zero-balance order, or resume to continue an attempt after a pending client action. Each action accepts only its own fields. Only confirm_payment_intents accepts completion_behavior. A pay action without payment_source is valid only when the outstanding balance is zero. To continue a resumable attempt, send action: resume with order_payment_attempt_id and a new Idempotency-Key. A Tap to Pay reader returns requires_action, is_resumable true, and a card_presentment pending action with stripe.terminal_payment_intent authority for the Stripe Terminal SDK. After the app collects and confirms, resume reads the outcome: authorization or capture applies it, processing keeps the attempt processing, and no card or a decline keeps it requires_action with the same authority. A decline updates last_payment_error without ending the attempt; cancel to give up. An exact retry of the original request with its Idempotency-Key returns the stored response if the request completed, or recovers the same attempt if it was interrupted. Payment intents with manual capture return an active authorization instead of settling immediately. A replay preserves the original HTTP status and domain result. Replays return no URL token or Stripe client secret; pending_actions is empty when action authority was stripped. Read the attempt to recover its current permitted actions. Read GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/payment-attempts/{order_payment_attempt_id} for the attempt's current state.

x-flint-conditional-scopes.when: Required when a payment source or selection has credential_type reader.

get.description: Returns payment attempts for the order, newest first. Checkout-session callers see only attempts created by their own session. A list filtered by idempotency_key omits pending_actions; read the attempt by ID to get them. Default order: started_at descending, then order_payment_attempt_id descending.
Returns one durable payment attempt for the order. Checkout-session callers can read only attempts created by their own session.

post.description: Cancels an active order payment attempt, its unsettled payment legs, and its attempt-owned holds.

Creates a payment intent owned by the order. For online payments, collect a source using payment_collection, then submit it through payOrder. With payment_options [card_present], no payment_collection is returned; send a reader credential through payOrder. This route requires commerce.orders.write; standalone payment-intent routes require payments.payment_intents.write.

get.description: Downloads a numbered receipt for an order with collected money, covering successful payment intents and gift card redemptions, including payments and refunds. Orders paid only by manual cash, check, or wire invoice payments return 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason unsupported_state; download the invoice PDF instead. Mixed orders list only successful payment intents and gift card redemptions. Available under either order_receipts email delivery mode. Buyer and seller identity is frozen on the first snapshot write; payments, refunds, and branding are current.

post.description: Marks a paid inventory failure as resolved after an operator has completed manual inventory remediation.

Queues a receipt for a paid order, including gift card payments and settled payments, and returns the order unchanged. Send email to choose a recipient, or omit it to use the order's email. If no receipt email is on file, email is required when your credential can set it. Otherwise, the request returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason configuration_required. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Checkout credentials can send only to the address on file. If no address is on file, checkout credentials can send to at most three distinct addresses over the order's lifetime. Receipts sent for this order through this route count toward this limit, including failed deliveries and receipts sent with a secret API key. Merchant callers can choose any address.

get.description: Lists package records, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then package_id descending.

post.description: Creates a package record under a shipment. Change package status through its lifecycle action routes, such as POST /v1/packages/{package_id}/mark-shipped; this endpoint records package-level carrier, tracking, label, measurement, and external correlation fields. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Retrieves one package by ID.

patch.description: Updates non-lifecycle package fields such as carrier, tracking, expected_delivery_at, label access, measurements, metadata, and caller-owned external references. Descriptive fields can be corrected until the package is voided, regardless of shipment or fulfillment status. Corrections never email the buyer. Package status cannot be patched directly. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Lists order line quantities contained in packages. Default order: created_at descending, then package_item_id descending.

post.description: Adds an order line quantity to a package. Total active package item quantities cannot exceed the parent fulfillment line-item quantity.

delete.description: Removes an order line quantity from a package while the package is still mutable.

get.description: Retrieves one package item by ID.

patch.description: Updates a package item quantity or metadata while the package is still mutable.

post.description: Performs one action from the package's supported_actions. mark_shipped accepts carrier, service_code, tracking_number, and tracking_url; present fields replace tracking before the status change and shipped email in one transaction. Omitted tracking is unchanged and null is invalid. Other actions reject tracking fields. mark_shipped, mark_in_transit, and mark_out_for_delivery optionally set expected_delivery_at; send null to clear it. Delivery preserves the estimate as history. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

Voids a package before carrier handoff and appends a package timeline event. Voided package items no longer count against fulfillment package allocation capacity. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Lists partner app installs on the authenticated merchant, across live and test mode. Requires a live API key. Default order: partner_app_install_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Disconnects a partner app from the authenticated merchant: revokes the install, its environment grants, its refresh tokens and linked API keys, and deletes linked webhook endpoints. The app is sent partner_app_install.revoked with revoked_by: merchant. A new request against an already revoked install returns empty ended-access arrays. Unlinked API keys and webhook endpoints keep working. To reconnect, install the app again.

get.description: Returns partner apps owned by the authenticated merchant. Default order: partner_app_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Creates a partner app owned by the authenticated merchant. A live API key or a live dashboard session is required.

delete.description: Archives a partner app (soft delete). The app stays readable with status archived; it cannot be installed, exchange tokens, or receive events, and its client ID is never reused. Revoke every active install first; pending installs are revoked with the app. Delete the app’s webhook endpoints separately.

get.description: Returns a single partner app owned by the authenticated merchant. A live partner app token can read its own app, without Flint-Merchant-Id or Flint-Sandbox-Id; another app's ID returns 404 as an unknown ID does.

patch.description: Updates a partner app owned by the authenticated merchant. Send only the fields to change. permission_manifest replaces the whole manifest and requires expected_version. An existing permission can drop scopes but not gain them; removing or narrowing a permission narrows existing environment grants immediately, and tokens issued with the removed scopes stop working. Adding a permission changes no install until the merchant authorizes again. Setting client_secret_enabled to true issues a first secret when secret authentication is disabled; only this response and its same-credential idempotent replay return that secret. Setting false ends current and previous secrets immediately. A Dashboard session needs fresh identity verification to enable secret authentication, including on replay.

post.description: Records that the authenticated credential accepted the current version of Flint's platform terms for the app: the signed-in user for a Dashboard session, or the API key. Flint also records the time, IP address and user agent. supported_actions lists accept_platform_terms while the current version isn't accepted. Accepting a version the app already accepted returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied. When this meets the app's last platform requirement, platform.status becomes pending_review in the same write and Flint sends partner_app.updated.

get.description: Lists active and removed credentials, ordered by partner_app_credential_id ascending. Default order: partner_app_credential_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Registers an immutable public key, JWKS URL, or workload identity for client assertion authentication. An app can have at most 20 active credentials. Dashboard callers need fresh identity verification. Replace a credential by creating a new one, then removing the old one.

delete.description: Soft-removes the credential and immediately stops its use for client authentication. The credential remains readable. Removing an already removed credential returns it unchanged.

get.description: Returns a credential, including a removed credential.

Returns installs for a partner app owned by the authenticated merchant. Each active grant that can read the merchant profile carries `merchant_readiness`: whether the installed merchant can take payments and receive payouts in that environment, and how many requirements are due. Use it to find merchants who still need to finish onboarding without exchanging each install’s token. A live partner app token can list its own app's installs, with the same filters and summaries as the owner; a merchant-bound token lists at most its merchant's install. Default order: partner_app_install_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

Returns a single install for the installing merchant, the partner app owner, or a live partner app token for the app. A merchant-bound token reads only its merchant's install; other installs return 404. For the app’s owner and its tokens, each active grant that can read the merchant profile carries `merchant_readiness`, the installed merchant’s payments and payouts readiness in that environment.

post.description: The installing merchant, the partner app owner, or a live partner app token for the app can revoke a single test or live environment grant for an install. A live token can revoke a test grant. A merchant-bound token can revoke only its merchant's grants; other installs return 404. This revokes linked API keys and deletes linked webhook endpoints in that environment. Revoking the last grant also revokes the install and ends its remaining links. Unlinked keys and endpoints keep working.

The installing merchant, the partner app owner, or a live partner app token for the app can revoke an install and all of its environment grants. A merchant-bound token can revoke only its merchant's install; other installs return 404. The owner and the app's tokens record revoked_by partner_app, and a token records no revoked_by_user_id. This also revokes linked API keys and deletes linked webhook endpoints. Unlinked keys and endpoints keep working. Reinstalling does not restore ended access.

Rotates an existing client secret, returned once. An app without a secret returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued. Issue its first secret with PATCH /v1/partner-apps/{partner_app_id} and client_secret_enabled: true. The previous secret keeps working until previous_secret_expires_at: 24 hours by default, or the time in expire_previous_secret_at, up to 7 days. Send a time at or before now to stop the previous secret immediately, for example when it leaked. Rotating again during an overlap ends the older secret at once.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of payment intents for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_intent_id descending.

post.description: Creates a standalone payment intent for the authenticated merchant and returns it flat in data with payment_collection guidance for online payments. Create order-owned payment intents with POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/payment-intents.

get.description: Returns a single payment intent by ID. Unverified fee fields are omitted; read the intent again later for verified fees. For a standalone payment intent in requires_action, call confirm with credential_type attached to retrieve current_payment_action.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update while status is requires_payment_method, requires_confirmation, requires_action, or requires_capture. In processing, succeeded, canceled, or expired it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `in_progress` or `terminal_status`, with the status in `error.details[].current_status`. amount_money can change only while status is requires_payment_method and before the first confirmation attempt; after that, create a new payment intent. customer_id can change only while status is requires_payment_method, and receipt_email only while it is requires_payment_method or requires_confirmation. Send null to clear tip_money, external_reference_id, receipt_email, or all metadata; amount_money and customer_id cannot be cleared. Order-owned intents accept only metadata and external_reference_id; amount_money, tip_money, customer_id, and receipt_email return INVALID_REQUEST with one NOT_ALLOWED detail per field. This route doesn't attach a payment source: send the buyer's credential to the confirm route.

get.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history for a payment intent. Read the payment intent or referenced resource for authoritative state; this log does not replace webhooks or a ledger. Use sort_direction=asc for a chronological timeline. Page tokens are bound to the payment intent, merchant, environment, activity_type filter, and sort direction. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_intent_activity_id descending.

post.description: Cancels a standalone or order-owned payment intent. Read supported_actions for the actions its stored state accepts. Canceling a hold moves all of capturable_money to released_money, and nothing is charged. A processing payment intent fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `in_progress`; refund a succeeded one instead. Flint derives the owning order payment attempt. A leg held by an active order payment attempt may be refused. Omitted cancellation_reason stays absent. A fresh request for a canceled or expired payment returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied; a same-key retry replays or recovers its original result. A checkout credential can cancel only its own order leg, with requested_by_customer or abandoned when a reason is supplied.

Captures a standalone or order-owned payment intent in requires_capture. Omit amount_money to capture all of capturable_money, or send a smaller amount for a partial capture. Send final_amount_money and tip_money instead to collect the final bill plus a tip in one charge; with request_overcapture and overcapture.status available, that total can exceed the authorization up to overcapture.maximum_capturable_money. On an order's payment, the bill is at most the payment's share of the order (its authorization minus its tip), the order releases the difference, and the tip becomes the payment's part of the order's tip. Flint releases the uncaptured remainder in the same request, and a payment intent can be captured only once. amount_money on the payment intent keeps the requested amount; captured_money and released_money record the result. Affirm payments can only be captured in full. Flint derives the owning order payment attempt; order_payment_attempt_id is not accepted. An expired authorization is refreshed before capture and refused with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status or authorization_expired. A fresh request for an already captured payment returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied; a same-key retry replays or recovers its original result.

Confirms a standalone payment intent. For the first confirmation, send credential_type stripe_confirmation_token, token, payment_method, or reader with its matching credential; a missing credential returns INVALID_REQUEST. After the buyer completes current_payment_action, call this route again with credential_type attached to continue the same payment attempt. Flint confirms again only if the processor still requires it, and otherwise returns the current payment intent. Unverified fee fields are omitted. On a Tap to Pay reader, requires_action returns current_payment_action with action_type card_presentment and stripe.terminal_payment_intent. Retrieve, collect, and confirm that payment with the Stripe Terminal SDK, then confirm with credential_type attached to read the outcome. A decline leaves the payment requires_action with last_payment_error so the app can collect another card; cancel to give up. current_payment_action is null when no buyer action is needed. It can also be null while status is requires_action if Flint cannot produce the action yet; call confirm again with credential_type attached. Order-owned payment intents return 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason order_owned and supported_actions; pay them through POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay using remediation.next_actions.

Queues a receipt for a succeeded payment intent and returns the payment intent unchanged. For an order-owned payment intent, sends the order receipt. Once sent, the receipt appears as a receipt_sent payment intent activity. Send email to choose a recipient. Omit email to use the order's receipt address for an order-owned intent, or receipt_email then the customer's email for a standalone intent. If no receipt email is available, email is required. The saved receipt email stays unchanged. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Standalone sending is limited to once every five minutes per payment intent; order receipt sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Retry with the same idempotency key to replay the result without sending again.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of payment links for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_link_id descending.

post.description: Creates a payment link for the authenticated merchant. Line items may use fixed prices, buyer-adjustable amounts, and buyer-adjustable quantities.

get.description: Returns a single payment link by ID. With expand=sales_summary, includes gross paid totals and refunded totals per currency.

patch.description: Updates a payment link. To replace line items, custom fields, or delivery methods, send the complete array with `expected_version`.

get.description: Returns the sanitized buyer-facing payment-link snapshot and a private resolution context for this browser operation.

post.description: Creates a buyer checkout session from an active payment link. Catalog-backed modifier availability is frozen onto the checkout session and selected modifiers are resolved onto the backing order. For a retry after an uncertain response, reuse the original idempotency key and resolution_context.

get.description: Returns payment method domains ordered by payment_method_domain_id ascending in the selected Flint environment. Page tokens are opaque, bind to the list parameters, and return a validation error when invalid or mismatched. Default order: payment_method_domain_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Registers one exact domain or subdomain for Apple Pay and Google Pay in the selected Flint environment, then validates its wallet readiness.

get.description: Returns one environment-scoped payment method domain and its Apple Pay and Google Pay readiness.

patch.description: Turns the domain on or off. Reads never check again with the provider; they return the last result. Sending status active registers the hostname on your current payment account, turns it on, and checks again any wallet that isn't active, so send it to check a domain again. Sending status inactive turns wallet buttons off for the hostname.

get.description: Lists payment methods in every status except archived, newest first. Filter by status=active for the cards you can charge. Optionally filter to a customer. Filter by usage off_session to list the payment methods a subscription, automatic invoice, or default payment method can use. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_method_id descending.

post.description: Initiates saving a payment method and returns the client setup payload needed to complete setup on the frontend.

delete.description: Deletes a saved payment method so it can no longer be used for future payments. Returns the payment method with status archived, including when it was already archived.

get.description: Returns a single payment method by ID.

Lists payment reviews, most recently opened first. A review opens when a `review` rule matches a payment the bank approved. Every status is included unless you filter by `status`. Default order: opened_at descending, then payment_review_id descending.
Retrieves a payment review. Expand `payment_intent`, `order`, or `customer` to include them.

post.description: Approves the payment and closes the review with `closed_reason: approved`. Approving never captures: capture a manual-capture payment yourself before `authorization_expires_at`. Approving a review you already approved returns it unchanged.

Declines the payment and closes the review with `closed_reason: declined`. Flint cancels an uncaptured authorization, or refunds the remaining captured amount (captured minus earlier refunds) to the original payment method with reason `fraudulent`. The review is closed once the decline completes. If the refund already failed, the review is `open` again with `last_resolution_failure` set. While the refund is still processing, the decline is accepted but not complete; wait for `payment_review.closed` or `payment_review.reopened`.

get.description: Lists splits where you are either party, newest first, then by payment_split_id descending. Read splits you collected or received, with your own credentials and money_movement.payment_splits.read. Install tokens can't read splits. Test splits are in the collecting merchant's sandbox and the seller's test grant's sandbox. Consumers include marketplace payment pages and seller reconciliation. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_split_id descending.

Read splits you collected or received, with your own credentials and money_movement.payment_splits.read. Install tokens can't read splits. Test splits are in the collecting merchant's sandbox and the seller's test grant's sandbox. Consumers include marketplace payment pages and seller reconciliation.

Returns a paginated list of payout destinations available to the authenticated merchant. The account owner adds a destination in the `payouts` embedded component, opened with POST /v1/merchant-account-sessions; Flint never takes bank details through the API. Default order: created_at descending, then payout_destination_id descending.

delete.description: Archives the payout destination and returns it with `status: archived`. It stays readable by ID. You can't delete the active default destination; make another destination the default with PATCH /v1/payout-settings first. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

get.description: Returns one payout destination by ID.

patch.description: Updates mutable metadata and settings for a payout destination. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

get.description: Returns payout settings that control default payout behavior for the authenticated merchant.

patch.description: Updates mutable payout settings for the authenticated merchant, including the default payout destination for each currency. Changing defaults requires expected_version, and each new default must be an active destination in its currency. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of payouts with optional filters for status, currency, destination, method, and timing. Default order: created_at descending, then payout_id descending.

post.description: Creates a payout from an available balance to an eligible payout destination. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

get.description: Returns one payout by ID, with optional related payout and payout destination expansions.

post.description: Cancels an eligible payout before it leaves Flint-controlled processing and returns the resulting payout.

get.description: Lists your partner apps' platform fee ledger, newest occurred_at first, then by platform_fee_balance_transaction_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: occurred_at descending, then platform_fee_balance_transaction_id descending.

Returns one entry of your partner apps' platform fee ledger. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list.
get.summary: Get a platform fee balance transaction

get.description: Lists your partner apps' platform fee balances, one per partner app and currency, newest first. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: time Flint opened the balance (descending), then platform_fee_balance_id descending.

Lists payouts from your partner apps' fee balances to your merchant balance, newest first, then by platform_fee_payout_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: created_at descending, then platform_fee_payout_id descending.

Returns one platform fee payout. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list.

Lists the platform fees your partner apps charged, newest first, then by platform_fee_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: created_at descending, then platform_fee_id descending.

Returns one platform fee. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list.

Lists price lists. Archived lists are excluded unless the status filter explicitly names archived. Results default to created_at descending, with price_list_id descending as the tiebreak. Default order: created_at descending, then price_list_id descending.

post.description: Creates a merchant-only price list. Currency is immutable. A customer segment can belong to only one unarchived list, including inactive lists.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a price list, releasing its segment assignments, and returns its full snapshot with status archived. A list referenced by customers returns RESOURCE_IN_USE. Repeating DELETE returns the same archived snapshot; a stale expected_version still returns VERSION_CONFLICT.

get.description: Returns a price list by ID, including archived lists. Price lists and their segment assignments are merchant-only.

patch.description: Updates only the fields supplied. Send customer_segments: [] to clear segment assignments. Inactive lists remain assignable but do not provide prices. Send expected_version to reject a stale write. Archived lists cannot be changed.

get.description: Lists the variant prices in a price list. Filter by variant_id or product_id. Results default to created_at descending, with price_list_price_id descending as the tiebreak. Default order: created_at descending, then price_list_price_id descending.

post.description: Atomically adds 1 to 500 variant prices. on_variant_conflict defaults to return_existing; update replaces an existing price and its full schedule. Each addition reports created, existing, or updated. Returns 201 if any price was created, otherwise 200. One changed batch advances the list version once. A list holds up to 10,000 prices.

delete.description: Permanently removes this variant price from its list and returns the parent price list with its new count and version. expected_version fences the parent price list. Repeating without the original Idempotency-Key returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

get.description: Returns a variant price and its complete quantity schedule within this price list.

patch.description: Updates a variant price or its quantity schedule. Omit quantity_price_breaks to preserve it; send [] to clear it. The resulting complete schedule must remain valid. expected_version fences this child price; an actual change also advances the parent list version once.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of products for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then product_id descending.

post.description: Creates a product, the catalog item buyers purchase through orders, checkout, payment links, and subscriptions. Send `name`, `product_type`, and `variant_mode`. A `simple` product takes one `default_variant`; an `optioned` product takes `options` and `variants`, each variant selecting one value for every option. Price, SKU, and inventory settings live on variants. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`, and a category handle that doesn't exist fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

delete.description: Archives a product and returns its final state. Returns the archived resource as a read does. Deleting an already archived resource returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references. A stale `expected_version` fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT` and the `current_version`, even when the resource is already archived.

get.description: Returns a single product by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to product-parent fields. When category_handles is present, it replaces the full category list; send [] to clear it. Sellable price, SKU, and inventory live on variants. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: List product options. Default order: position ascending, then option_id ascending.
Returns one option of a product, such as size or color, with its values and position.
List product variants. Default order: position ascending, then variant_id ascending.

post.description: Adds a variant to a product that has options. The variant selects one value for every option. Two variants can't select the same combination, and a SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses is refused; both fail with `ALREADY_EXISTS`. A product without active options fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `configuration_required`: change a simple product through its default variant instead. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

delete.description: Archives a variant and returns its final state. Returns the archived resource as a read does. Deleting an already archived resource returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references. A stale `expected_version` fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT` and the `current_version`, even when the resource is already archived.

get.description: Returns one variant of a product, including its price, SKU, selected options, inventory settings, and delivery configuration status.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a variant: only the fields you send change. A SKU or barcode that another variant or bundle already uses, or an option combination that another variant selects, fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`. Changes to name, price, SKU, and similar fields apply to new checkouts, links, and plans; existing orders keep what they were charged. Setting the variant inactive, or changing its price currency, fails with `RESOURCE_IN_USE` while an open order, checkout session, active payment link, subscription, subscription plan, or active bundle uses it. Send `expected_version` to reject the update when the variant changed since you read it. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of promotion codes in every status, ordered by created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending. Archived codes are excluded unless status=archived. Default order: created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending.

post.description: Creates a code for a promotion whose `redemption_type` is code; adding a code to an automatic promotion fails with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A code that another resource already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

delete.description: Archives a promotion code. The code remains readable with status archived. Returns the archived resource as a read does. Deleting an already archived resource returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references.

get.description: Returns a single promotion code by code ID. Archived codes remain readable, including codes of an archived promotion. Fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` when the code does not exist or belongs to another merchant or environment.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to a promotion code. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of promotions for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then promotion_id descending.

post.description: Creates a promotion: a discount that applies to qualifying orders automatically or when the buyer enters a promotion code. Send `name` and `application_method`; `redemption_type` chooses between automatic and code-gated, and a code-gated promotion can create up to 100 `codes` with it. Eligibility rules, a schedule, a redemption limit, and exclusivity are optional. The promotion is active unless you send `status: inactive`. A code that another resource already uses fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`.

delete.description: Archives a promotion and returns it as a read does. Deleting an already archived promotion returns it again without changing its version or `updated_at`, sending a webhook, or checking references.

get.description: Returns a single promotion by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to promotion fields. application_method, schedule, exclusivity, and combines_with patch by subfield presence. Omitted fields retain stored values; null clears only nullable fields. Sending a different application_method.type replaces the effect while preserving omitted shared settings, including discounted_item_rules. A redeemed promotion can't change its `discount_class` or `application_method` type; the update fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `field_locked`. Archived promotions cannot be changed. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `archived` when the resource, or the parent it belongs to, is archived. The error names the archived resource and its `current_status`.

get.description: Lists readers newest first, then by `reader_id`. Archived readers are listed only when the `status` filter names `archived`. Default order: created_at descending, then reader_id descending.

post.description: Readers are payment hardware at a location: a Stripe Reader S710 or S700 your server sends payments to through Flint (`smart_reader`), or a phone that takes Tap to Pay in your app with the Stripe Terminal SDK (`tap_to_pay`). A reader is separate from a device, which records the register or phone that runs your app. Registers a smart reader with its pairing code, or a Tap to Pay reader for a phone, at a location with a complete US address. A pairing code works once, so send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key returns the same reader. Registering needs no live payment readiness; payments on the reader do. Sends `reader.created`.

delete.description: Archives a reader and returns it with `status: archived`. A smart reader is unregistered from Stripe shortly after, so its hardware can be paired again; a Tap to Pay reader stops getting connection sessions at once. Refused with `RESOURCE_IN_USE` while a payment is presented on the reader. Archiving an archived reader returns it unchanged. Sends `reader.archived`.

get.description: Returns a reader, including an archived one, with the payment presented on it now in `active_payment_intent_id`.

patch.description: Changes a reader's `name`, `device_id` (`null` clears it) and `metadata` (merged by key). A reader's `type` and `location_id` never change: to move a reader, archive it and register it again at the new location. An archived reader can't change. Sends `reader.updated`.

post.description: Tap to Pay readers only. Creates a fresh single-use Stripe Terminal connection token for the reader's location: return `client_session.stripe.connection_token` from the SDK's `fetchConnectionToken` callback, and pass `client_session.stripe.location_id` to `TapToPayConnectionConfiguration`. Each call creates a new token, including a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`. The token works with readers at the reader's location, not only this phone, so your server decides which phone gets which session. Keep your credential on your server.

Sandbox only. Presents a Stripe test card on a simulated reader (registered with `registration_code: simulated-s700`) for the payment presented on it, so the result arrives the way a real tap's does. Returns the reader. A live credential gets `403 FORBIDDEN` with reason `test_mode_required`.
post.summary: Simulate a card on a reader

get.description: Returns a paginated list of refunds for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then refund_id descending.

post.description: Creates a refund for an issued credit note on a paid invoice, an order, a payment intent, a captured gift card redemption, or a gift card load. Set refund_type to credit_note with credit_note_id to refund credit; omit amount_money to refund all available credit, resolved when Flint accepts the request. Credit-note refunds return card and bank payments collected through Flint, largest remaining first; gift card value is not refunded through credit notes yet. Set refund_type to full for the full remaining refundable amount, amount for an explicit amount_money, or targets for named line items, charges, and taxes. To refund a gift card redemption made outside a Flint order, set refund_type to amount and send one tender_allocations entry per redemption, with no order_id. A created refund is returned even when processing fails; inspect `status` and `failure_reason`. A same-key replay returns the original refund without another money attempt. This is a financial operation.

get.description: Returns a single refund by ID.

patch.description: Updates refund metadata and external_reference_id.

post.description: Resolves a remembered buyer token without sending a code. Only a checkout credential can call this route, including after the checkout ends. A merchant key is refused. The email is always masked. code_channel is sms or email when this checkout can request a recognition code for the buyer, and null otherwise; it does not consider code caps. An unknown, expired, ended, replaced, other business's, or other sandbox's token returns the same 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

Ends the remembered identity named by the body token and returns its final masked resource with no supported actions. Only a checkout credential can call this route, including after the checkout ends. A repeat without an idempotency replay returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Forgetting never changes saved cards.

get.description: Authorizes the stable Flint download URL and redirects to a short-lived private file URL.
Lists reports using opaque pagination. Default order: created_at descending, then report_id descending.

post.description: Creates an idempotent asynchronous CSV report. receivables_aging_v1 takes as_of_date instead of interval timestamps, with a cutoff at the earlier of the end of that local day and report creation. For interval reports, interval_end_at may be at most the same local time 366 calendar days after interval_start_at in timezone, and must not be in the future. Poll the returned report until it succeeds or fails.

get.description: Returns one report and its terminal download or failure details when available.

Returns summary-only API request, webhook event, webhook delivery attempt, and image mutation entries for a single public API resource. The caller must have developer.resource_timelines.read and the matching read scope for the requested resource type. Default order: occurred_at descending, then resource_timeline_entry_id descending.
List merchandise dispositions. Omitting return_id lists dispositions across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_disposition_id descending.
Retrieve one disposition with its type, destination, quantity, status, and any linked inventory effect.

post.description: Cancel a disposition that has not started its inventory effect. Cancellation is refused once the effect is processing.
Retry a failed disposition with the same immutable intent. Disposition and effect identities are preserved, so a retry does not move stock twice.

get.description: List inspection observations. Omitting return_id lists inspections across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_inspection_id descending.
Retrieve one inspection with its line items, findings, and current or superseded observation status.

post.description: Record the accept or reject outcome for inspected quantity. expected_version compares against the inspection version. Accepted quantity becomes dispositionable and satisfies after_inspection release timing.

get.description: List Return policies with their status. Include the current revision with expand=current_revision. Default order: created_at descending, then return_policy_id descending.

post.description: Create a Return policy with its first revision. The policy ID is stable across revisions, and each published revision is immutable.

delete.description: Archive a Return policy so it is no longer evaluated or offered. Archiving is permanent.

get.description: Retrieve one Return policy. Supports expand for current_revision.

patch.description: Update policy identity fields or set status to active or inactive. Rules live on revisions, so changing a window, fee, or scope means publishing a new revision.

get.description: List every published revision of a Return policy. Default order: created_at descending, then return_policy_revision_id descending.

post.description: Publish a new immutable Return policy revision while preserving the stable policy identity. Send the policy's current version as expected_version to reject a concurrent policy edit or publish.

get.description: Retrieve one immutable policy revision, including the exact rules a Return was evaluated against.

post.description: Preview return eligibility or resolution amounts without creating a Return or reserving quantity. Set mode to eligibility or resolution and send the matching input object.

get.description: List Return reasons, including Flint-provided defaults and merchant-defined reasons. Flint reasons have a created_at of 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, so they follow your own. Default order: created_at descending, then return_reason_id descending.

post.description: Create a merchant Return reason buyers can select. Buyer reasons are distinct from inspection findings, decline reasons, and Refund reasons. Flint handles and all existing merchant handles, including archived reasons, are reserved. A conflicting handle fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`.

delete.description: Archive a Return reason so it can't be selected on new Return lines. Returns that recorded it keep its name and handle. Flint reasons can't be archived; set status to inactive instead. An archived reason's handle stays reserved.

get.description: Retrieve one Return reason with its handle, category handles, and status.

patch.description: Update a Return reason. Send null to clear description. A present category_handles array replaces the existing set. Set status to active or inactive to control availability. Flint reasons accept only status and expected_version; create your own reason to use different wording. Use DELETE to archive a merchant reason.

get.description: List merchandise receipts. Omitting return_id lists receipts across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_receipt_id descending.
Retrieve one merchandise receipt with its line items and its current or superseded observation status.

post.description: Establish the Return line identity for receipt quantity that arrived without one. expected_version compares against the receipt version. Unverified quantity counts toward no line and releases no release timing gate until it is verified.

get.description: List resolutions. Filter by corrects_return_resolution_id to retrieve the correction history for a resolution that already settled. Default order: created_at descending, then return_resolution_id descending.
Retrieve one resolution with its amounts, adjustments, execution blockers, and linked refunds, payments, and replacement order. Supports expand for those links.

patch.description: Update a proposed resolution before confirmation. A present line_items, replacement_line_items, or adjustments array replaces that collection and requires expected_version.

post.description: Cancel a resolution and release the line value it reserved. A failed resolution can be canceled only when it never created a Refund, PaymentIntent, or Order, or when it is an unpaid exchange or replacement. Effects that already succeeded are undone with a compensating correction instead.
Confirm a proposed resolution and freeze its economic facts. Execution can remain pending behind line-qualified execution blockers.
Release a confirmed resolution that is waiting on a manual release. Available only while action_reason is manual_release.

Retry a failed resolution. For gift_card_refund_destination_required, send gift_card_refund_destination: new_gift_card to persist the destination before starting the new attempt. The override is accepted for refund, exchange, and corrections of resolutions other than store_credit. A new attempt starts, historical payment and refund IDs stay on the resolution, and a late event from an earlier attempt cannot settle the new attempt. Fails with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED, with the line's current_status, when a Return line the resolution covers is no longer approved, such as after it was canceled, and with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when an approved line no longer has the quantity the resolution covers. Retry is available only when failure_code allows it, and supported_actions includes retry in that case. A failure that retry cannot fix fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; cancel the resolution instead.

get.description: List Returns for the merchant, filtered by order, customer, status, decision, merchandise, resolution, or creation window. Filter by idempotency_key to recover a create whose response never arrived. Set sort_direction to asc for oldest first. Default order: created_at descending, then return_id descending.

post.description: Create a requested Return. Every line needs the return_reason_id of an active reason. With an API key, a Return that no policy matches stays available for merchant review rather than failing creation.

get.description: Retrieve a Return with its line items, policy evaluation, financial summary, and completion blockers. Supports expand for the order, customer, receipts, inspections, dispositions, resolutions, shipments, and each line item's reason and fulfillment.
