patch.description: Update caller-owned fields on a Return. Only external_reference_id and metadata are writable. Send optional expected_version to reject a stale Return version; every other change goes through a decision, operation, or resolution command.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's email about a Return carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the Return and its order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in. Withdrawing the Return needs the buyer to sign in. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the Return. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`, and for a Return whose order has no customer, with reason `configuration_required`. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

get.description: Read the merchant history of a Return for timelines and audit. Read the referenced resources for current state. Activities are newest first by default; use sort_direction=asc for chronological order. Default order: created_at descending, then return_activity_id descending.

post.description: Cancel a Return before any merchandise or value work commits. Cancellation is refused once a receipt, inspection, disposition, or resolution exists.
Complete a Return whose completion_mode is manual. The call fails while completion_blockers is non-empty. Automatic Returns complete themselves when the final blocker clears.

Record one decision for every requested line atomically, then open the Return. To defer a line, decline its quantity or remove it with DELETE /v1/returns/{return_id}/line-items/{return_line_item_id} and open a separate Return for it. Omit completion_mode to use the shared pinned policy mode, or automatic when none sets a mode; disagreeing policies require an explicit completion_mode. completion_blockers reports uncovered approved quantity as resolution_not_selected alongside blockers for unfinished resolutions. Start from each buildable pinned policy proposal or the no-policy defaults, replace every supplied decision field, fill release_timing, and validate the result. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually, or choose no_monetary_action.

Record an auditable merchandise disposition from either a receipt line or an inspection line. Read dispositions with `GET /v1/return-dispositions?return_id=` or expand `return_dispositions` on `GET /v1/returns/{return_id}`.

Record an immutable inspection observation. Corrections supersede an earlier inspection instead of editing physical history. Read inspections with `GET /v1/return-inspections?return_id=` or expand `return_inspections` on `GET /v1/returns/{return_id}`.

get.description: List the line items on a Return with their quantity counters, eligibility, frozen display identity, and return value. Default order: created_at descending, then return_line_item_id descending.

post.description: Add a line item to a requested Return. The response is the updated Return, not the new line.

delete.description: Remove a line item from a requested Return. Send optional expected_version as one query parameter to fence against the parent Return version. The response is the updated Return.

get.description: Retrieve one Return line item, including its quantity counters and the reason the buyer selected.

patch.description: Update a requested Return line item. Send null to clear buyer_note or requested_resolution_type. The response is the updated Return.

post.description: Cancel approved quantity on a Return line item. Quantity already received, inspected, dispositioned, or reserved by a resolution, including a failed one, cannot be canceled, and the conflict response names what is blocking it. Omit handback_quantity to lower the expected handback only as far as the canceled quantity requires. An explicit value cannot leave more merchandise expected than the remaining approved quantity.

Waive the inspection requirement on a Return line item so received quantity can be dispositioned and resolved without an inspection observation. Received quantity on a waived line satisfies after_inspection release timing.

Record decisions, receipts, inspections, dispositions, and resolutions for an existing requested or open Return in one request. On a requested Return, send one decision for every requested line; missing decisions fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached`. Omit completion_mode to use the shared pinned policy mode, or automatic when none sets a mode; disagreeing policies require an explicit completion_mode. On an open Return, omit decision and completion_mode to keep committed values, or send those values unchanged; changed values fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `field_locked`. completion_blockers includes resolution_not_selected for any uncovered approved quantity alongside blockers for unfinished resolutions. A line can be processed here only while it has no receipt, inspection, disposition, or resolution; otherwise ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED has reason unsupported_state and param line_items[i].return_line_item_id. A receipt location that differs from a line's committed location fails with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED, reason field_locked, and param receipt.receiving_location_id. Missing receipt or receipt.receiving_location_id fails with INVALID_REQUEST and detail REQUIRED. For each line, received_quantity must equal its committed return_required_quantity. Send inspection exactly when the line requires inspection, with acceptance_status accepted. Refunds, payments, replacement orders, and inventory updates complete asynchronously. expected_version is optional and checked only when sent. If the Return has changed since that version, the request fails with VERSION_CONFLICT. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; on a decision, send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually; on a resolution, choose another resolution_type, such as no_monetary_action, and reimburse the buyer another way. Requires an idempotency key and all three scopes: commerce.returns.write, commerce.returns.operations.write, and commerce.returns.resolutions.write.

Record an immutable merchandise receipt observation. Corrections supersede an earlier receipt instead of editing physical history. Read receipts with `GET /v1/return-receipts?return_id=` or expand `return_receipts` on `GET /v1/returns/{return_id}`.

Reopen a completed Return to record late compensating facts. Reopening sets completion_mode to manual, so complete the Return again with /complete once completion_blockers is empty. Confirmed money movements are never edited backward, so a monetary fix is a new correction resolution.

Propose a buyer-value outcome for approved quantity. Creating a resolution reserves line value. Confirmation is what freezes it and starts its effects. Read resolutions with `GET /v1/return-resolutions?return_id=` or expand `return_resolutions` on `GET /v1/returns/{return_id}`.

get.description: Lists risk lists, newest first, including Flint's default block lists. Archived lists appear only when status includes archived. Default order: created_at descending, then risk_list_id descending.

post.description: Creates an empty list. Rules refer to it by alias, which can't be changed or reused, even after the list is archived. item_type decides how values are validated and compared.

delete.description: Archives a list you created. Fails with `RESOURCE_IN_USE` while an active rule names it. Flint-managed lists fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`. Archived lists can't be used by rules or edited. Items can still be added to and removed from active Flint-managed lists.

get.description: Retrieves a risk list. item_count is its current number of values.

patch.description: Renames a list you created. Flint-managed lists fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`. Items can still be added to and removed from active Flint-managed lists.

get.description: Lists a list's values, newest first. Default order: created_at descending, then risk_list_item_id descending.

post.description: Adds up to 500 values, each validated and normalized for the list's item_type. The additions array reports each value's outcome: values already on the list come back as existing, so a batch is safe to resend. The response is `201` when at least one value was added and `200` when none were. Payments see the change from the next attempt.

delete.description: Removes a value from a list permanently. Payments see the change from the next attempt.

get.description: Retrieves one value on a list.

post.description: Validates a rule without saving anything. Send mode inline with action and predicate to check a draft; add risk_rule_id to check them as an edit to that rule. Send mode stored_rule with risk_rule_id, to check the saved rule, optionally overriding action or predicate. An omitted or null override keeps the saved value. Requires risk.read. Rule content issues produce a preview with `is_valid: false`, every issue in order, `analysis` null, and empty `warnings`. A valid rule returns analysis and any warnings about how the change would affect evaluation. List reference issues are reported at the list_alias path. A new rule at the active-rule limit gets a risk_rule_limit_reached warning. A malformed request fails with `INVALID_REQUEST`, and an unknown `risk_rule_id` fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Proposing a different action or predicate for a Flint default rule fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `managed_externally`.

get.description: Lists risk rules, newest first, including Flint's default rules. By default, includes active and inactive rules. Archived rules appear only when status includes archived. This isn't the order Flint evaluates them in. Default order: created_at descending, then risk_rule_id descending.

post.description: Creates a rule that applies from the next payment attempt. Flint validates the predicate and checks every list before activating the rule. The rule is active unless you send status: inactive. An environment can have 100 active rules, counting Flint's defaults. To check a draft without saving it, use POST /v1/risk-previews.

get.description: Lists the attributes a predicate can read in this environment, with each one's value type, operators, and the stage it becomes available. An attribute with is_available: false can't be used yet. Payment intent metadata is also readable as payment_intent_metadata.{key}, which isn't listed.
get.summary: Get the risk rule attribute registry

delete.description: Archives a rule. It stops running at once and can't be changed or restored. Flint's default rules can't be archived; set them inactive instead.

get.description: Retrieves a risk rule. The issues array lists anything that stops Flint from evaluating it.

patch.description: Changes a rule's action, predicate, description, or status, and increases its version. Send expected_version to avoid overwriting another edit. Flint's default rules accept only status. Activating a rule validates it again.

get.description: Returns the merchant's sandboxes. Flint guarantees a default test sandbox for every merchant. Use an onboarding session during setup or a live credential afterward. Test credentials cannot list sandboxes. Default order: is_default descending, then created_at descending, then sandbox_id descending.

post.description: Creates a new empty test sandbox for the current merchant. Send `issue_test_key: true` to also receive a test key bound to it; this also requires `accounts.api_keys.write`.

delete.description: Archives a non-default sandbox and frees its original name for reuse. A sandbox whose reset stopped after deletion started can be archived; its previous and new data are then deleted in the background.

get.description: Returns a single sandbox by ID. A test credential (API key, CLI login, or workload token) can read only the sandbox it is bound to; any other `sandbox_id` gets 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

post.description: Deletes a sandbox's data and keeps its identity and connections. The default sandbox can be reset too. A test credential (API key, CLI login, or workload token) with `developer.sandboxes.write` can reset only the sandbox it is bound to; any other `sandbox_id` gets 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and the credential keeps working after the reset. The sandbox keeps its `sandbox_id`, name, and `is_default`; every credential bound to it, including API keys, workload identities, CLI logins, and connected app installs; its webhook endpoints with their secrets and API versions; its test payment account and readiness; its payment method, checkout, and custom domains; and its processing fee assignments. Everything else is deleted: catalog, customers, orders, payments, invoices, subscriptions, test clocks, settings, locations, risk lists, request logs, events, deliveries, and idempotency keys. Returns the same sandbox with `status` `active` and a new `updated_at`. Requests that start while the reset runs get 409 `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` with reason `sandbox_resetting`; retry them after Retry-After. A second reset while one is running gets 409 `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`. Failed resets retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 60 minutes, with at most eight attempts. Each attempt counts when it starts, including interrupted attempts. `reset_failed_at` records when a reset stops. If deletion has not started, the sandbox keeps its previous data and accepts requests again. If deletion has started, requests get 409 `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` with reason `sandbox_reset_failed`, without Retry-After. Reset it again to resume, or archive a non-default sandbox. A successful reset clears `reset_failed_at`. Requests already running when the reset started finish against the old data, and their results don't survive the reset. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the recorded response; a new key resets again. Each sandbox allows one reset every 10 seconds and 500 resets per UTC day, shared by every credential that can reset it; past either limit the request gets 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with Retry-After, and a same-key retry doesn't count again. See the [sandboxes guide](/docs/guides/sandboxes#reset-a-sandbox).

get.description: Returns the settings stored for the authenticated merchant in this environment.

patch.description: Applies a sparse patch to merchant settings. See each field for how it is patched. A partner app install token can't send `checkout.enabled_payment_options`, `customer_account.buyer_capabilities`, `inventory.origin_policies`, `invoices.autopay_retry_policy`, `invoices.default_collection_mode`, `invoices.default_invoice_payment_term_id`, `invoices.payment_policy`, `invoices.remit_to_address`, `payment_limits`, `payments.statement_descriptor`, `subscriptions.default_billing_schedule_owner`, `subscriptions.dunning_end_action`, `subscriptions.dunning_retry_days`, `subscriptions.external_dunning_end_action`, `tax`, or `tax_identity`, or null for `checkout`, `customer_account`, `inventory`, `invoices`, or `subscriptions`; each returns `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with a `NOT_ALLOWED` detail whose `param` names the field.

get.description: Returns the authenticated merchant's settings for this environment with Flint's defaults filled in.
Lists shipment execution records, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then shipment_id descending.

post.description: Creates an outbound shipment for fulfillment_id or a return shipment for return_id. For outbound shipments, include 1 to 20 packages to create the parcels atomically and return their IDs. Set each package's status to shipped to report handoff in the same call. Return shipments cannot include packages.

get.description: Retrieves one shipment execution record by ID.

patch.description: Updates shipment metadata and caller-owned external references. Shipment status is derived from package statuses and cannot be patched directly. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied.

post.description: Voids a shipment before carrier handoff and voids all child packages that have not shipped. The action appends timeline events for the shipment and affected packages. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

get.description: Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_delivery_migration_id descending.

post.description: Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion.
post.summary: Move subscribers to another delivery method

get.description: Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion.

Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion. Default order: subscription_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.
get.summary: List subscriptions that could not be moved

get.description: List subscription offers. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_offer_id descending.

post.description: Create subscription offer. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms.

delete.description: Archive subscription offer. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms.

get.description: Get subscription offer. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms.

patch.description: Update subscription offer. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of subscription plans for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_plan_id descending.

post.description: Creates a subscription plan: the recurring price and terms customers sign up to. Send `name`, `currency`, the billing interval, and at least one line item from your catalog. An active plan accepts new signups; an inactive plan refuses them with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` while existing subscriptions keep renewing. A free trial isn't allowed on a plan with lines that ship.

delete.description: Permanently archives a subscription plan from active or inactive status. Returns RESOURCE_IN_USE while active subscriptions, active payment links, or open checkout sessions reference the plan. To stop selling a plan while keeping its subscribers, set status to inactive.

get.description: Returns a single subscription plan by ID.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to mutable subscription plan fields. Setting status to inactive returns RESOURCE_IN_USE while active payment links use the plan. Open checkout sessions do not block this change; buyers in those sessions are refused with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED when they pay. Send line_items with expected_version to replace the plan's line items; omit line_items to keep them.

post.description: Estimates the next renewal, a plan change, or a promotion attachment, or evaluates a proposed subscription, delivery destination, or delivery method update without saving changes. next_renewal returns current recurring promotions, shipping, and tax for the next charged cycle. plan_change uses the same checks and pricing as change-plan, including unused paid item credit for billing_starts now or prorated_now. quantity_change accepts the change-quantity inputs and previews the same prorated charge without changing the subscription. promotion_apply uses the same checks as applying a promotion and returns the proposed attachment and the renewal estimate for its first_cycle; its refusals return HTTP errors. Tax is null when tax can't be calculated yet; a tax service failure returns 502 EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR. Malformed JSON, unknown fields and request-level problems (a missing or unsupported mode, fields that belong to another mode) return 400. Create mode returns SubscriptionCreatePreview with first_charge, first_period_charge, and recurring estimates, all null when validation prevents pricing. first_charge is the first Flint collection, including any separate setup fee; recurring is the first normal full-period collection without setup fees. With prorate_first_period, the prorated first period is first_charge, or first_period_charge when a setup fee is collected first, and recurring is cycle 2 at the end of that period. is_valid means valid and priceable inputs, not payment readiness. Card validation matches creation, including cardless imports. In create mode, every problem with the proposed subscription is returned in errors with is_valid false, including CUSTOMER_EMAIL_REQUIRED when the customer has no email and promotion refusals under subscription.promotions. A create preview attaches no promotions and counts no uses. A preview does not reserve inventory or guarantee a future shipping rate.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of subscriptions for the authenticated merchant. Subscriptions without a next_billing_at never match next_billing_after or next_billing_before, and sort last with sort_by=next_billing_at in either direction. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_id descending.

post.description: Creates a subscription for a customer outside checkout. Send `customer_id`, the `terms` (a subscription plan or subscription offers), and `billing_start`, which says whether billing begins now, on a later date, or continues a period the buyer already paid elsewhere. Renewals charge `payment_method_id`, or the customer's default payment method when you omit it. Free trials without an upfront charge and `imported` starts can begin without a card when the customer has no default payment method; other starts fail with `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `payment_method_id`. A setup fee or other creation-time charge requires a card; scheduled starts also require one. Bind a card before `payment_method_due_at`: a trial without one cancels at that boundary without an attempted charge, while an imported subscription follows its normal dunning schedule. Flint requests the card three days before the boundary, or when a shorter trial begins. A default payment method that can't be used fails the request on every start. The payment method must belong to the customer, be active, and allow charges without the buyer present. A plan that is not active fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. Subscriptions require a customer with an email address in both customer account modes; otherwise creation returns 409 CUSTOMER_EMAIL_REQUIRED. Optional promotions (up to five) freeze current terms and qualify against the projected order for first_cycle. Imports alone accept consumed_cycles to carry over the buyer's used allowance. Attaching counts one promotion use and, when sent by code, one code use.

get.description: Returns a single subscription by ID. A paid checkout session's credential can retrieve only the subscription created by its source order. Checkout credentials cannot expand related resources.

patch.description: Updates metadata, external_reference_id, payment_method_id, delivery, billing interval, quantity, cancel_at_period_end: false to undo a scheduled cancellation, or scheduled_plan_change: null to keep the current plan. Send billing_interval and billing_interval_count together. A billing_schedule update must be the only mutable field. Delivery, cadence and quantity changes apply to future unpaid renewals. Send expected_version to reject concurrent changes. Schedule a cancellation with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel, change the plan with /change-plan, and manage lines through the line-items collection. A card whose setup hasn't finished fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached`. Once setup finishes, send a new request with a new idempotency key.

post.description: Creates a link to one subscription in your Flint-hosted customer account, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. Omit purpose or send subscription_view for read-only access without a sign-in. Send subscription_manage to also let the buyer cancel, pause, or undo a scheduled cancellation, subject to your store's policy and the subscription's state. subscription_manage requires commerce.subscriptions.write; subscription_view requires commerce.subscriptions.read. Neither purpose permits other subscription changes or access to another subscription. Both work for 14 days or 5 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same idempotency key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. Dashboard sessions may create view links when the staff member can view subscriptions; subscription_manage requires permission to manage subscriptions. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `merchant_hosted_customer_accounts`. Send no request body, an empty object ({}), or an optional purpose and return_url. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an idempotency key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with the request ID before sending a new request.

Cancels a subscription and records who asked, why, and when in cancellation_details. With cancel_immediately: true it ends now. Otherwise, trialing ends at trial_end_at, active at current_period_end_at (or now when a renewal delivery hold has expired), and past_due at next_retry_at instead of that retry. Scheduled, incomplete, paused, and past_due without next_retry_at require cancel_immediately: true or fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `period_end_unavailable`. Paid deliveries extend a scheduled cancellation to the last paid delivery when it is later. A merchant can cancel immediately without an automatic refund. A buyer cannot cancel immediately while prepaid deliveries remain and period-end cancellation is available; the refusal reason is `prepaid_deliveries_remaining`. Read scheduled_cancel_at for the scheduled end time. A buyer's cancellation follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

Replaces the subscription's lines and recurring options with the active target plan's current terms. Paired lines keep their quantities unless line_items overrides them. Pair by the same plan line on the same plan, then variant or bundle, then the only line on each side. Unpaired target lines use their plan quantity. If an adjusted current line cannot be paired, send quantities for every target line; otherwise the request fails with quantity_not_carried before any change. With billing_starts next_renewal, changes terms now without charging and keeps the current period and next billing date. With billing_starts prorated_now, charges the new terms for the rest of the current period, less unused paid item credit, while keeping the billing period and anchor; the resulting interval must stay unchanged. With billing_starts now, charges a new period and credits unused paid item time after promotions; the plan changes only when payment succeeds. If the credit exceeds the new item charge, choose next_renewal. Omit interval and quantity to keep their current values; the target plan must offer them. Contract terms and existing recurring promotions are preserved. Requires Idempotency-Key; retry with the same key to recover the same result. Returns status 200 for a decline, with a closed unpaid order, failed order_payment_attempt, and unchanged subscription. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error and update the subscription payment method before trying again. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change. After a confirmed CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION with billing_starts now, refresh the subscription and send a new Idempotency-Key.

Changes the subscription quantity multiplier, existing line quantities, or both, with the chosen billing timing. billing_starts is required: prorated_now charges now, next_renewal changes quantities immediately without charging, and period_end schedules them for the next billing boundary in scheduled_plan_change. Cancel pending quantities with PATCH scheduled_plan_change: null. A pending change locks quantity edits with plan_change_scheduled. Keeps the current billing period, next billing date, anchor and completed cycles. Omitted quantities stay unchanged. Send quantity or 1 to 50 distinct line_items. With prorated_now, a shipping line cannot be changed, and quantity cannot be supplied when any subscription line ships. Physical quantities can use next_renewal or period_end. Digital line quantities can be changed on a subscription with other lines that ship; its shipping lines stay unchanged and this charge creates no shipment or shipping charge. Quantities that do not charge can still be updated with subscription PATCH or the line-item routes. Requires Idempotency-Key; retry with the same key to recover the original outcome. Returns 200 on decline with a closed unpaid order, failed order_payment_attempt, and unchanged subscription. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error before trying again. The order and order_payment_attempt are null when the net charge is zero. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change. If the outcome remains uncertain, retrieve the subscription and its orders; contact Flint support with the original key and request ID when those reads cannot establish the result.
Adds a catalog variant or bundle to future subscription renewals. Current prices and delivery eligibility are checked before the line is saved. Already-created orders keep their lines.

delete.description: Removes a line from future subscription renewals. The final line cannot be removed. Send expected_version as a query parameter to reject a concurrent change.

patch.description: Updates a subscription line for future renewals. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change. Already-created orders keep their lines.

post.description: Pauses a subscription immediately. pause_duration_cycles counts delivery intervals on prepaid subscriptions and billing intervals otherwise; omit it for an indefinite pause. A pause with a duration resumes automatically at scheduled_resume_at. Repeating the stored pause length returns the paused subscription; a different length returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason field_locked and param pause_duration_cycles and requires resuming first. A buyer's pause follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

get.description: Returns a subscription's manual payment retries, newest first. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_payment_retry_id descending.

post.description: Starts one manual collection attempt on a past-due subscription. Send no body, or an empty object. Poll the returned retry for the outcome.

get.description: Returns one durable manual subscription payment retry.

post.description: Attaches a promotion to a subscription for future charged cycles. Send exactly one of promotion.promotion_id or promotion.promotion_code. first_cycle defaults to completed_cycles + 1, or completed_cycles + 2 while past_due, and cannot exceed completed_cycles + 120. Use replace_promotion_id to replace an active or scheduled promotion from first_cycle forward. The unpaid past_due order keeps its price. Promotion terms are frozen when attached; reattachment keeps consumed cycles. Offer promotions cannot be replaced. Requires commerce.subscriptions.write.

Removes 1 to 5 unique active or scheduled promotions from a subscription. Future renewal orders omit them; paid orders and the unpaid past_due order keep their discounts. Removal keeps consumed cycles for reattachment and does not return a promotion use. Offer promotions cannot be removed. Requires commerce.subscriptions.write.

Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires an idempotency key; retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt, including when the payment is declined. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

Asks Flint to resume a paused subscription. The request is accepted while the subscription is still paused, with `resume_requested_at` set. Flint then makes it active, or past_due while an overdue period is collected, and sends subscription.resumed. While prepaid deliveries remain, resuming makes no charge and shifts later deliveries and the next charge by the length of the pause. If Flint can't resume it, it stays paused, resume_requested_at clears, and Flint sends subscription.updated. Any other status fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. To undo a scheduled cancellation, PATCH the subscription with cancel_at_period_end set to false.

While prepaid deliveries remain, defers the next delivery and next charge by one delivery interval without consuming a delivery. Otherwise skips the next renewal without charging or shipping and moves the next billing date forward by one billing interval. A Flint-owned schedule keeps its billing_anchor_day, including when the skipped date falls in a shorter month. Available while the subscription is active, is not set to cancel at the end of its period, and has a next billing date.

get.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Default order: created_at descending, then tax_calculation_callback_id descending.

post.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Creates an inactive callback and immutable revision 1. signing_methods defaults to ["jwt"]. Verify the JWT with Flint's public JWKS, aud equal to tax_calculation_callback_id, and body_sha256 over the exact request bytes. HMAC secrets are returned only once when hmac is selected.

delete.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Archives the callback. Select another callback or clear tax.calculation_callback_id before archiving the selected callback.

get.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported.

patch.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Configuration and signing-method changes require expected_version and publish an immutable revision. Configuration fields are patched individually. Change status on its own. A callback selected by tax.calculation_callback_id cannot be deactivated.

post.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Sends a signed connection_check request. A 2xx response succeeds unless it sets a Content-Type other than application/json or its body is larger than maximum_response_bytes. Runs for inactive and active callbacks without changing the circuit breaker.

Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Issues an HMAC secret and adds hmac when needed. Returns the new secret once. The previous secret remains valid during the same overlap as delivery callbacks.

Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Sends a signed synthetic tax_calculation request with test true and empty line_items and charges. The response must echo tax_calculation_evaluation_id and return empty line_item_calculations and charge_calculations. Runs for inactive and active callbacks without changing the circuit breaker.
post.summary: Send a tax callback test delivery

get.description: Returns the environment's automatic sales tax connection, including before a record exists. Read the disclosure and status_reason to learn what connect needs. Business-detail changes, temporary provider pauses and registration date boundaries are computed at read time and do not advance version or send webhooks.

post.description: Records the seller's attestation and creates or completes the tax account from verified business details and the default line-item tax category in settings. Syncs registrations and removes tax-account copies of deleted registrations. Reconnect retains the tax account and does not turn the default tax setting back on. A rejected stored registration returns attention_required with registration_rejected. Successful configuration marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete and advances their versions. A same-key retry resumes setup without creating another account; unconfirmed account creation requires support. Retrieve the connection after a lost response.

Turns automatic tax off while retaining the tax account and registrations for reconnecting. Choose tax_default_behavior explicitly: turn_off stops adding tax to new orders, checkout sessions and renewals that inherit the default; keep leaves the default unchanged, refuses those orders and holds renewals for retry without charging buyers or starting dunning. Payment links that explicitly enable automatic tax are refused when creating a checkout session with either choice. Settings are updated first when needed, then the connection is disconnected and open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice snapshot become incomplete. Issued invoice snapshots are unchanged. A same-key retry resumes after settings were changed; after a lost response, retrieve the connection and disconnect again if needed.

get.description: Returns independent tax registrations ordered by state ascending, then tax_registration_id ascending. Removed registrations never list. After a lost create response, filter by state and match the start_date sent by the create. Default order: state ascending, then tax_registration_id ascending.

post.description: Saves one US state registration for a non-overlapping, inclusive date window. Start_date may be up to 365 days ahead; end_date is optional. Before the connection is active, saves locally as pending without creating a tax account. On an active connection, syncs the registration in this request. Acceptance of a registration effective today marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete, advancing their versions. Scheduled registrations do not invalidate calculations. A definitive rejection before a tax-account registration exists removes the pending registration and leaves working tax and orders unchanged. If a tax-account copy exists or may have been created, rejection cleanup marks those open orders incomplete and advances their versions. Successful cleanup leaves the connection active. An uncertain outcome keeps the registration pending and the connection active; retry with the same key to resume without duplicating the registration. If the key is lost, filter the list by state and match the submitted start_date, delete the pending registration and create again after deletion succeeds.

delete.description: Hard-deletes a pending, rejected or scheduled registration and returns its final snapshot with status removed. While disconnected, deletes locally and records tax-account cleanup for the next connect. Otherwise, removes a possible tax-account copy first. If earlier creation is unconfirmed, an empty tax-account registration list does not prove the copy is absent: EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR keeps the local registration. Retry the same request with the same idempotency key until the copy can be identified and removed. Provider failure retains the local registration. An online deletion of a pending or rejected registration that removes existing or possibly created tax-account coverage marks open calculated automatic-tax orders without an issued invoice incomplete and advances their versions. Scheduled and disconnected deletions do not invalidate calculations. Scheduled deletion removes its tax-account copy immediately unless disconnected, without pausing automatic tax or invalidating calculations. Active and ended registrations cannot be deleted. A later GET fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

get.description: Returns one saved tax registration. Removed registrations return RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

patch.description: Updates locally without a tax-account call. Pending and rejected registrations allow registration_number, start_date and end_date; registration_number and start_date require a connection that is not active. Scheduled and active registrations allow only end_date. A pending or rejected registration whose tax-account copy exists or may have been created cannot change start_date; delete it and create it again. Ended registrations cannot be changed. End_date must be on or after start_date and today (UTC); null clears it before the registration ends. Date windows in the same state cannot overlap. To replace an active registration number, set its end_date, then create a replacement starting the next day. Changing end_date does not invalidate calculations made today. An empty patch is invalid.

get.description: Sandbox only. Lists the sandbox's test clocks, newest first, then by `test_clock_id`. Archived clocks are listed only when the `status` filter names `archived`. Default order: created_at descending, then test_clock_id descending.

post.description: Sandbox only. Creates a test clock stopped at `frozen_at`, with status `ready`. Customers created on it, and their subscriptions, read its time instead of real time.

delete.description: Sandbox only. Archives the test clock. It stays readable by ID, never advances again, and no new customer can be created on it. Customers and subscriptions already on it are not changed: they keep the clock's `frozen_at` as their current time, so their subscriptions don't bill again. Cancel those subscriptions first if you want them canceled, or reset the sandbox to remove everything. Deleting an archived clock returns it unchanged.

get.description: Sandbox only. Returns a test clock in this sandbox, including an archived one.

post.description: Sandbox only. Moves the test clock forward to `frozen_at`. Flint accepts the request and returns the clock in status `advancing`, then moves the clock's customers and their subscriptions to `frozen_at`, running the billing that falls due along the way, in order. Flint sends `test_clock.ready` when the advance finishes, or `test_clock.failed` if it can't finish. You can also read the clock with `GET /v1/test-clocks/{test_clock_id}` until its status is `ready` or `failed`. One advance reaches at most two years, or two billing intervals of any subscription on the clock that isn't canceled, whichever is earlier.

get.description: Lists individual event tickets, newest first by default. Merchant credentials never receive admission codes. The checkout credential of a paid checkout session lists only its own order's tickets: it must send that order_id, may not send other filters, search, sort or expand, and receives admission_code on every ticket that isn't voided, unless the credential came from a launch URL a merchant read or requested after payment. Any other order_id returns 403, as reading another order does. Default order: created_at descending, then ticket_id descending.

post.description: Looks up an admission code in the authenticated merchant and environment, including voided tickets. ASCII lowercase, spaces and hyphens are accepted; O maps to 0 and I/L to 1. Malformed codes return 400 INVALID_VALUE; an unknown or foreign code returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND at admission_code. The code is never returned.

get.description: Returns an individual ticket. Merchant credentials never receive its admission code. The checkout credential of a paid checkout session reads only its own order's tickets, without expand, and receives admission_code unless the ticket is voided or the credential came from a launch URL a merchant read or requested after payment; another order's ticket returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

patch.description: Sets the attendee name. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; send null to clear the name. Sending the current name changes nothing and keeps the version. A voided ticket returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason unsupported_state.

post.description: Admits an issued ticket. Concurrent check-ins of one ticket admit it once: the others return 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied and current_status checked_in. A stale expected_version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT first, so scanners usually omit it. With admission_code the check-in method is admission_code, and the code must be the ticket's current code: a wrong code returns 400 at admission_code and changes nothing. Without a code the method is manual. A voided ticket returns reason unsupported_state. There is no event-time window. The code is never returned or logged.

Replaces the ticket's admission code and returns the new code once, in admission_code. The old code stops working immediately. Use it to deliver tickets yourself with send_ticket_emails turned off. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key within 24 hours returns the code again while the ticket is unchanged since this rotation; after any later change, including another rotation, it returns the ticket without admission_code. A voided ticket returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason unsupported_state.

Returns a checked-in ticket to issued and clears checked_in_at and check_in_method. An issued ticket returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied; a voided ticket returns reason unsupported_state.

Permanently voids an issued or checked-in ticket and releases its seat: the payment link's total_quantity_sold drops by one in the same transaction. Like a refund release, this doesn't change the link's version or send payment_link.updated. Nothing is refunded and the order's ticketed_event doesn't change. A later full refund of the order releases only its remaining valid tickets. A voided ticket returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason already_applied.

get.description: Returns webhook deliveries, newest first (`created_at` descending, then `webhook_delivery_id`). Includes deliveries of synthetic test events. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_delivery_id descending.

post.description: Creates a delivery for a retained event and an endpoint that currently subscribes to it, then attempts delivery now. A failed attempt starts the automatic retry schedule. Each event and endpoint pair can have only one delivery. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

get.description: Returns one endpoint delivery and its current retry state. Global partner-source records are invisible in sandbox mode; a direct reference returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

Returns the attempts recorded for a specific webhook delivery. Global partner-source records are invisible in sandbox mode; a direct reference returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Default order: attempt_number ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

post.description: Sends the event to the delivery's endpoint now, including while automatic retries are pending. A failed resend doesn't change the automatic schedule. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

get.description: Returns a page of webhook endpoints for the authenticated merchant. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Filters selecting only partner_app or installed_merchants return an empty collection. Direct resource reads of partner-source records return 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND in sandbox mode; exact-ID list filters return an empty collection when no visible records match. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_endpoint_id descending.

post.description: Creates a webhook endpoint. signing_methods defaults to ["jwt"]. A shared secret is issued and returned once only when hmac is included. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the webhook endpoint and returns it with status deleted. Its pending deliveries are suppressed. The endpoint cannot be retrieved afterward, and its past deliveries keep its webhook_endpoint_id. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

get.description: Returns a single webhook endpoint by ID. The signing secret is omitted after creation. Global partner-source records are invisible in sandbox mode; a direct reference returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

patch.description: Updates a webhook endpoint's URL, description, status, subscribed events, event sources, signing methods, or pinned API version. Only the fields you send change. Sending `enabled_events`, `event_sources`, `installed_merchant_modes`, or `signing_methods` replaces that whole list and requires `expected_version`; a stale version fails with `VERSION_CONFLICT`. Adding `hmac` when no secret exists issues the first secret and returns it once. Removing `hmac` deletes all shared secrets. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

post.description: Rotates an existing shared secret. An endpoint without hmac returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued; PATCH signing_methods to include hmac to issue the first secret. The secret is returned once. The replaced secret keeps signing deliveries until previous_secret_expires_at: 24 hours by default, or expire_previous_secret_at, up to 7 days. Send a time at or before now to stop the replaced secret immediately, for example when it leaked. Rotating again during an overlap ends the older secret at once. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

Sandbox only. Returns the exact delivery body and headers for an authorized sandbox endpoint without dispatching it. Requires webhooks.write and permission to read the event's resource. JWT signing must be enabled. Each call reauthorizes and creates a fresh five-minute bearer frame; receivers deduplicate webhook-id. Limited to one request per 200 ms and 10,000 per UTC day per endpoint, plus external-provider-action API quotas. The 200 ms throttle returns 429 with Retry-After; daily exhaustion returns 409 LIMIT_REACHED with limit and resets_at and no Retry-After. Signing fails closed if the shared quota store is unavailable. Responses are not cached or retained for idempotency. Previously issued JWTs remain usable until expiry after endpoint changes.

Creates and delivers a synthetic test webhook event to one active webhook endpoint. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

get.description: Returns every webhook event type you can use in enabled_events and event filters, with the event sources each type is valid for. Default order: event_type ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

Returns recent canonical webhook events for the authenticated merchant. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Filters selecting only partner_app or installed_merchants return an empty collection. Direct resource reads of partner-source records return 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND in sandbox mode; exact-ID list filters return an empty collection when no visible records match. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_event_id descending.

Streams canonical merchant webhook events created after the connection opens or after the supplied event ID. SSE event IDs are resumable webhook event IDs. Control records include ready, gap, withheld, and disconnect. Gap records indicate cursor_unavailable or payload_expired; withheld records hide payloads the caller cannot read. Backpressure emits disconnect with reason backpressure and resume_cursor identifying the last sent event, so clients can reconnect without losing events. A partner app token streams the installed merchant's events in the environment its grant covers, and sees a payload only for an event Flint forwards to installed-merchant endpoints whose read scope the grant holds; every other event is a withheld record.
Returns a specific webhook event for the authenticated merchant. Global partner-source records are invisible in sandbox mode; a direct reference returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

Returns identities in the authenticated environment, ordered by created_at descending and workload_identity_id descending by default. Archived identities are excluded unless status includes archived. Default order: created_at descending, then workload_identity_id descending.

post.description: Creates an active identity in the authenticated environment and validates issuer discovery. Dashboard callers creating live identities, or granting accounts.api_keys.write, accounts.workload_identities.write or commerce.gift_cards.secrets.write in any mode, need fresh identity verification. Other callers may grant only scopes they hold in this environment, and only a full-access key can grant those three.

delete.description: Soft-archives the identity and returns it with status archived. The identity remains readable by ID and cannot be reactivated. Repeating DELETE without a stale fence returns the archived identity without changing its version.

get.description: Returns an identity in the authenticated environment, including an archived identity.

patch.description: Updates mutable policy fields. expected_version is optional for scalar updates and required when claim_conditions or scopes is supplied. Arrays replace their entire value. Issuer and audience are immutable. Dashboard callers reactivating or widening live identities need fresh identity verification.

post.summary: An API key was created. The snapshot never includes its secret.

releases.overview: Balance transactions report fee charges as positive amounts (on a payment, the processing fee plus any add-on fees), name their timestamp `occurred_at`, and name the related resource in `related_resource` with `resource_type` and `resource_id`. Tax categories split into `line_item_tax_category` for items and `charge_tax_category` for charges, so the field name tells you which set of values applies.

changes.summary: Balance transaction fee charges are positive and fee credits are negative.
changes.action: Read a positive `fee_money` as a fee charged and a negative one as a fee returned. `net_money` is unchanged.

changes.summary: Balance transactions name their related resource in `related_resource`, with `resource_type` and `resource_id`.
Balance transactions use occurred_at for the transaction timestamp.
Tax categories use line_item_tax_category for items and charge_tax_category for charges.
changes.action: Replace `tax_category` with `line_item_tax_category` on product variants, modifiers, bundles, and line item taxes, and with `charge_tax_category` on delivery methods and charge taxes.
